      its logs/results are retained under `build/validation/`. See the Sphinx validation
      page for timing observations, LPF warnings, and untested GUI/hardware acceptance.

## Activity

    $ /bin/bash -lc 'cat new_approach/docs/{architecture,configuration,builds,simulation,validation,layout,environments,getting-started}.rst new_approach/Makefile; cat new_approach/buildsystem/model.py new_approach/buildsystem/cli.py new_approach/buildsystem/backends/diamond.py'
    status: Completed · exit 0
      Architecture and Python integration
      ====================================
      
      Make supplies convenient commands; :mod:`buildsystem.cli` parses their arguments.
      :func:`buildsystem.model.load_build` creates a validated :class:`buildsystem.model.Build`.
      :mod:`buildsystem.workflow` manages locks, regeneration, cleanup and provenance.
      :class:`buildsystem.backends.diamond.DiamondBackend` handles vendor project
      preparation and build Tcl.
      
      From ``new_approach/``, use the Python API without shelling out to Make::
      
         from pathlib import Path
         from buildsystem.model import load_build
         from buildsystem.workflow import build_program
      
         config = load_build(Path("/path/to/new_approach"), "tx30")
         artifacts = build_program(config)
      
      The ``root`` argument is the standalone workspace directory containing
      ``programs/`` and ``targets/``. Input paths cannot escape it. Build and simulation both
      read the same manifests and local VHDL copies under ``new_approach/programs/``.
      Each program directory also contains its LPF and cocotb testbench. Firmware outputs live under
      ``new_approach/build/<program>/<target>/diamond/``; simulation results live under
      ``new_approach/build/simulation/<program>/``.
      
      Importing these build modules does not invoke Diamond. Use workflow functions to retain
      locking and provenance guarantees; direct backend methods are lower-level helpers.
      Expected user/configuration failures raise :class:`buildsystem.model.BuildError`.
      The CLI reports them with a nonzero exit status.
      
      Build lifecycle
      ---------------
      
      A build holds a lock outside its disposable directory, checks generated settings
      for external changes, removes previous artifacts, and generates a fresh project.
      Diamond Tcl imports a copied strategy and references the authored files. Because
      Diamond treats ``def_top`` as an internal Tcl option, the generator writes that
      option into the generated LDF XML after Tcl saves the project.
      
      The backend runs synthesis, translation, map, PAR, PAR timing, Bitgen and Jedecgen.
      Vendor subprocesses receive no display variables and no interactive stdin.
      Success requires both nonempty exports from the fresh implementation directory,
      the required reported tool version, and unchanged input hashes across the build.
      Failure logs and intermediates remain available for diagnosis.
      
      ``build.json`` records hashes of HDL, LPF, strategy, manifests and frontend Python
      files; Git revision/status; selected device, options and tool version; the launcher
      path/hash; report and firmware hashes; completion time and the build-log path.
      It is an audit record, not a reproducible-build proof. The mounted Diamond
      installation and unpinned OS packages remain external state. Preserve the logs
      alongside artifacts when publishing a release. Firmware publication and hardware
      qualification remain a separate process.
      
      Extending the system
      --------------------
      
      Additional backends should implement project preparation, build execution and
      artifact collection while keeping board and program definitions separate.
      Currently backend selection rejects everything except Diamond; no placeholder
      FOSS implementation claims successful builds. Device-specific primitives require
      review before reusing programs on other families.
      
      Future work includes reviewed catalog expansion, shared logic/constraints,
      container digest/package pinning, hardware programming, FOSS and ispMACH backends,
      and separate PDF/SVG netlist analysis. Earlier design discussions and
      implementation records are available in :doc:`history`.
      Manifests and targets
      =====================
      
      Program manifest
      ----------------
      
      ``programs/<name>/<name>.toml`` explicitly lists inputs. Paths are relative to
      the manifest, must stay within the checkout, and must exist. No recursive source
      globbing is used. The catalog programs each declare ``SignalRouter`` and must
      be compiled separately. Their HDL is local to ``programs/<name>/`` and their
      LPFs are alongside them as ``<name>_constraints.lpf``. Each LPF is preserved separately, including
      its electrical settings and existing warnings; no shared constraint merging is
      performed.
      
      .. literalinclude:: ../programs/tx30/tx30.toml
         :language: toml
      
      ``name`` matches the directory and uses lowercase letters, digits and underscores,
      starting with a letter. ``top`` is the VHDL entity. ``standard`` is ``"1993"`` or
      ``"2008"``. ``sources`` is ordered and assigns each file to a VHDL library.
      ``testbench`` names the program-local ``<name>_tb.py`` cocotb file; the runner
      loads it explicitly rather than discovering unrelated tests.
      ``targets`` explicitly lists supported target names. The selected target must
      appear in that list. Exactly one authored LPF is supported in the first version.
      Constraint composition is deliberately rejected until conflict handling is
      implemented. Unknown fields, duplicate paths and unsupported backends are errors.
      
      Target manifest
      ---------------
      
      .. literalinclude:: ../targets/uz_dslot_xo2/target.toml
         :language: toml
      
      ``uz_dslot_xo2`` identifies the UltraZohm D-slot MachXO2 target. Its current
      hardware scope is the Rev05+ D-slot ``LCMXO2-2000HC-4TG100C``. The target name
      is separate from the backend and program. D-slot
      position belongs to the program's mapping or a future programming command;
      it is not a different toolchain. Only the specified XO2-2000 device is currently
      accepted. S2C, S3C and ispMACH are not implemented targets.
      
      ``diamond.strategy`` identifies the captured legacy strategy file, which is now
      an explicit input. ``diamond.version`` is the required version found in build
      reports. ``diamond.options`` maps Diamond Tcl strategy option names to string
      values. Example::
      
         [diamond.options]
         lse_opt_goal = "Balanced"
         par_place_effort_level = "5"
      
      VHDL standard is controlled by the program manifest; do not also set
      ``lse_vhdl2008`` here. Unknown vendor option names fail during preparation.
      The initial baseline preserves legacy options, including its preference-error
      handling. Review constraints and vendor warnings; do not interpret a successful
      process exit as proof of correct electrical assignments or timing closure.
      
      The initial catalog contains only ``tx30``, ``rx30`` and ``tx26_w_enable``.
      Existing program manifests also define the source for ``make new TEMPLATE=<name>``;
      there is no separate template metadata. Shared HDL extraction is a separate functional change.
      
      
      Future capability matching
      ---------------------------
      
      Capability matching is deferred. Neither ``capabilities`` nor ``requires`` is a
      current manifest field; the loader rejects these fields rather than ignoring
      them. Compatibility currently uses the program's explicit ``targets`` list.
      
      When multiple targets are supported, a target could advertise features such as
      ``machxo2``, ``s3c_safety_interface`` or ``internal_oscillator``, while a program
      could declare the features it requires. The loader would reject a selection
      unless all required features are available. This could catch incompatible
      program/board combinations before invoking a compiler.
      
      These labels would describe reviewed hardware and backend support. They would
      not generate HDL, enable physical features, inspect VHDL automatically, or make
      a program portable merely by changing a target flag. Reintroducing them would
      require defined meanings, reviewed target declarations, and validation tests.
      
      Target rename
      ---------------
      
      ``uz_dslot_xo2`` replaces the earlier name ``rev05_dslot``. CLI and Make defaults
      use the new name. Existing generated outputs under ``build/<program>/rev05_dslot/``
      remain historical local artifacts; new builds use
      ``build/<program>/uz_dslot_xo2/``. Earlier session records retain the original name.
      Build and author programs
      =========================
      
      Complete :doc:`environments` first. Commands below run from ``new_approach/``.
      The repository-root Makefile forwards the same commands here.
      
      Build the catalog::
      
         make list
         make doctor
         make check PROGRAM=tx30
         make build PROGRAM=tx30
         make build-all
      
      ``check`` validates inputs without Diamond. ``doctor`` also checks Tcl startup;
      it does not establish synthesis or export success. ``build-all`` processes the
      explicit catalog and returns failure if any catalog entry fails.
      
      Outputs are under ``build/<program>/<target>/<backend>/``:
      
      * ``project/``: generated LDF, strategy, Tcl, and tool intermediates.
      * ``logs/``: timestamped preparation/build logs, retained across builds.
      * ``artifacts/``: fresh ``firmware.jed``, ``firmware.bit``, reports and ``build.json``.
      * ``status.json``: latest attempt status.
      
      A failed build removes current artifacts and preserves logs. Build operations
      never program a device. Existing released firmware in legacy directories is
      preserved.
      
      Create a program
      ----------------
      
      Clone an existing program and edit the resulting files::
      
         make new NAME=my_adapter TEMPLATE=tx30
         # Edit my_adapter.vhdl, my_adapter_constraints.lpf and my_adapter_tb.py
         # inside programs/my_adapter/.
         make check PROGRAM=my_adapter
         make sim PROGRAM=my_adapter
         make build PROGRAM=my_adapter
      
      ``TEMPLATE`` names an existing program directory, defaulting to ``tx30``.
      Any valid program can be the source, including one you created yourself. The
      command copies its current authored files, renames the four primary files, and
      updates manifest references while preserving source order, libraries, target
      support, HDL entity names and testbench behavior. Additional local files are
      copied too; Python caches are excluded. There is no separate ``templates/`` tree.
      Inputs outside the source program directory must be localized before cloning.
      The clone is independent: future edits to the original do not update it.
      The generated manifest is ``programs/<name>/<name>.toml``. Creation refuses an
      existing destination. New programs are not automatically added to ``build-all``;
      review their behavior and constraints before adding them to
      ``programs/catalog.toml``.
      
      The ``tx26_w_enable`` program forwards channels 0–25 when FPGA channels 26–29 are
      0, 0, 1, 1 and ``reqsafestate`` is low. Its declared outputs 26–29 remain
      undriven, matching the legacy source. Review the reports when cloning this program.
      
      All commands are also available directly, for example::
      
         python3 -m buildsystem build --program tx30 --target uz_dslot_xo2
         python3 -m buildsystem --help
      
      GUI workflow
      ------------
      
      On a Linux host with a display and a native Diamond installation::
      
         make project PROGRAM=tx30
         make gui PROGRAM=tx30
      
      Generated projects reference authored HDL and LPF files using relative paths.
      Edits to those authored files persist. Verify the destination when saving from
      Spreadsheet View: an exported/generated LPF does not replace the authored LPF.
      Useful GUI changes to project membership or strategy must be transferred manually
      into manifests or the target strategy baseline.
      
      ``gui`` opens an existing project without regenerating it, preserving experiments.
      ``project`` and ``build`` regenerate settings and reject externally modified
      LDF/strategy/Tcl files. After transferring useful changes, discard generated work::
      
         make clean PROGRAM=tx30 DISCARD_PROJECT_CHANGES=1
      
      Ordinary ``make clean PROGRAM=tx30`` protects modified settings and removes only
      the selected generated directory. Authored inputs are preserved.
      
      Managed project/build/clean/GUI commands share a process lock. The GUI launcher
      must stay in the foreground until Diamond closes. A separately opened GUI cannot
      honor this lock; close it before starting a managed build. Container paths and
      host paths may differ: ``make project`` on the host can regenerate paths when
      needed. Native GUI interaction still requires the manual acceptance checks in
      :doc:`validation`.
      
      RTL simulation
      ==============
      
      The open-source simulation suite uses GHDL, cocotb, pytest, and GTKWave.
      It compiles the actual sources listed in the program manifests; Diamond and
      a license server are not required. Simulation currently covers ``tx30``,
      ``rx30``, and ``tx26_w_enable`` on the Rev05 D-slot target.
      
      Run the suite
      -------------
      
      Inside the Dev Container or with Docker available on the host (see :doc:`environments`), run from ``new_approach/``::
      
         make sim
         make sim PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable SEED=42
         make sim WAVE_FORMAT=fst
      
      ``make sim`` builds the cached image and runs the tests inside it. The root
      Makefile forwards the command. No host Python packages or GHDL are required. Both workflows consume the same manifests as
      :doc:`builds`; ``make test`` runs frontend regression tests, while ``make sim``
      executes the HDL tests. An unknown simulation program fails instead of silently
      running no tests.
      
      Inspect and reproduce failures
      ------------------------------
      
      Every simulation writes to ``build/simulation/<program>/``:
      
      * ``waves.ghw``: waveform containing the complete cocotb regression run.
      * ``compile.log`` and ``simulation.log``: compiler output and test assertions.
      * ``*.result.xml``: cocotb test results.
      * ``run.json``: random seed, simulator/Python versions, and source hashes.
      
      Paths here are relative to ``new_approach/``. The pytest summary is
      ``build/simulation/junit.xml``. CI uploads this directory
      even after failures. Download and extract the artifact, then open the waveform::
      
         gtkwave build/simulation/tx26_w_enable/waves.ghw
      
      Add the top-level data and safety signals from GTKWave's signal tree. GHW
      preserves VHDL types; ``make sim WAVE_FORMAT=fst`` produces smaller FST traces.
      The current tests are deterministic. ``SEED`` remains available in the runner
      and ``run.json`` for programs that later add randomized stimulus.
      Rerunning a program replaces its logs, results, and waveforms; copy
      artifacts elsewhere before comparing runs. Concurrent runs of the same program
      must use separate checkouts.
      
      Behavior under test
      -------------------
      
      Each program has one short, dedicated test function in its own ``<name>_tb.py``.
      There is no program selector or generic routing helper inside these files.
      All-zero, all-one, walking-one and walking-zero patterns check every data route.
      For each pattern, the safe-state request goes from 0 to 1 and back to 0.
      The enable-controlled program checks all 16 enable codes for each pattern.
      Pilot, carrier-ready, SCL and SDA are held at zero. Randomized transitions and
      exhaustive auxiliary-input combinations are omitted to keep these tests simple.
      
      ``tx30`` and ``tx26_w_enable`` force transmitted data low during a safe-state
      request. ``rx30`` continues receiving data during safe state, while deasserting
      ``slotok``. All three programs hold ``reqoe`` high. These distinctions are
      explicit test contracts, not a claim that every program has identical safety
      behavior. The four unused D-slot outputs of ``tx26_w_enable`` are not driven by
      the RTL and are not treated as valid data outputs in these tests.
      
      Why async is used
      -------------------
      
      Cocotb test functions are coroutines, so they use ``async def``. After assigning
      inputs, ``await Timer(1, unit="ns")`` pauses the Python test and lets the HDL
      simulator advance. The test then reads the settled outputs. This is simulation
      time, not a wall-clock sleep or a measured propagation-delay requirement.
      
      These tests execute sequentially and start no concurrent tasks. Plain helper
      functions that do not wait on the simulator can use ordinary ``def``. A VHDL
      native testbench could use ``wait for`` instead, but Python cocotb uses
      ``async``/``await`` for that coordination. See the
      `cocotb testbench guide <https://docs.cocotb.org/en/v2.0.0/writing_testbenches.html>`_.
      
      Extending verification
      ----------------------
      
      Place the testbench in ``programs/<name>/<name>_tb.py`` and reference it with
      ``testbench`` in ``<name>.toml``. ``make sim PROGRAM=<name>`` runs that module;
      without ``PROGRAM``, simulation selects the explicit catalog. Source order,
      top entity, and VHDL standard come from the existing manifests. The initial
      runner accepts only ``work`` sources; additional libraries need explicit
      compilation before elaboration.
      
      The three initial programs need no vendor primitives; their unused
      ``library machxo2`` declarations were removed from the program sources.
      For future oscillator/EFB users, introduce wrappers and explicit behavioral
      models. Do not silently replace hardware primitives with empty stubs. Model
      tests should cover reset, bus errors, and timing assumptions. RTL simulation
      does not replace implementation timing analysis or hardware validation.
      
      For software cosimulation, retain UltraZohm's Ceedling unit tests and add a
      separate integration layer: host-compiled C driver, hardware-access adapter,
      cocotb transactions, and simulated HDL. Blocking C calls need a bridge that
      lets simulator time advance. Drivers accessing FPGA IP through AXI also need
      that IP or a documented model between the driver and CPLD. No C bridge or
      processor emulator is included in this initial suite.
      
      References
      ----------
      
      * `cocotb simulator support <https://docs.cocotb.org/en/v2.0.0/simulator_support.html>`_
      * `GHDL waveforms <https://ghdl.github.io/ghdl/using/Simulation.html>`_
      * `UltraZohm software unit tests <https://docs.ultrazohm.com/software/unit_tests/unit_tests.html>`_
      * `UltraZohm resolver interface <https://ultrazohm.org/ip_cores/uz_resolverIP/uz_resolverIP.html>`_
      Validation and acceptance
      ===========================
      
      From ``new_approach/``, run ``make test`` for frontend regressions, ``make sim``
      for HDL behavioral tests and waveforms, and ``make docs`` for a strict Sphinx
      build. The repository-root Makefile forwards all three commands. Actual tool validation uses ``make build-all`` with the mounted
      Diamond installation and its valid license. No command programs hardware.
      
      Tooling tests and hardware testbenches
      ---------------------------------------
      
      ``toolchain_tests/`` tests the Python build tooling itself. ``make test`` runs
      its regression suite without Diamond. The separate
      ``toolchain_tests/validate_diamond.py`` checks cloning and firmware generation
      with licensed Diamond; legacy comparison is optional.
      
      Hardware behavior is tested by ``programs/<name>/<name>_tb.py`` through
      ``make sim``. Those testbenches are kept with their programs.
      
      Routing semantics to preserve
      -------------------------------
      
      * ``tx30`` gates all 30 adapter outputs with ``not reqsafestate``.
      * ``rx30`` forwards adapter inputs directly to FPGA outputs; its ``slotok``
        reflects the safe-state request, but its data routing is not gated.
      * ``tx26_w_enable`` additionally requires the 0, 0, 1, 1 enable pattern on FPGA
        channels 26–29. Adapter outputs 26–29 are declared but undriven in the legacy HDL.
      
      All three drive ``reqoe`` high in their present source. Template generation and
      migration retain these definitions without refactoring safety logic.
      
      Manual release checks
      -----------------------
      
      1. Review pin/electrical reports against the board and adapter mapping.
      2. Review combinational delays and vendor warnings. These routing LPFs do not
         define a timing acceptance budget, so successful builds do not mean timing
         closure. Clocked programs need explicit clocks and timing requirements.
      3. Compare unchanged legacy and generated-project builds using the same tool,
         HDL, constraints and strategy. Ignore container paths and timestamp headers
         when comparing payloads and reports.
      4. Open the generated LDF in native Diamond. Edit authored VHDL and save; verify
         the authored LPF destination in Spreadsheet View, then rebuild headlessly.
      5. Relocate the checkout, regenerate/reopen the project, and repeat the build.
      6. Perform adapter-specific functional and hardware validation before release.
      
      The shared CI workflow in ``.github/workflows/toolchain.yml`` runs frontend
      regressions and HDL simulation in the simulation image, then retains results and
      waveforms from ``new_approach/build/simulation/`` even after failures. The same job builds the shared guides and API reference inside that image and
      uploads the HTML site.
      Diamond builds are validated locally with the mounted installation; the CI
      workflow does not supply a vendor license.
      
      Tool validation results for this implementation are recorded below. Native GUI interactions and hardware behavior require their respective
      environments and must not be inferred from synthesis.

      * ``make docs``: Sphinx 4.3.2 HTML build passed with warnings treated as errors.

      * Isolated legacy builds matched generated builds in JEDEC programming records,

      * A new ``tx30``-derived program built in a separate checkout path containing

      Run ``python3 toolchain_tests/validate_diamond.py`` after ``make build-all`` to repeat the

      The maximum default enumerated path delays in this run were 13.905 ns for

      Existing warnings needing adapter/board review:

      The session's vendor startup failed license host-ID detection inside the agent

      Consolidation checks
      ---------------------
      
      After moving the implementation into ``new_approach/``, the root forwarding
      commands passed all 11 frontend regression tests and all three simulation cases.
      The strict Sphinx build includes both workflow guides and the simulator runner API.
      The Dev Container recipe paths and simulation-container mount/build commands were
      checked against the new layout. Container images and remote CI jobs were not
      launched during this reorganization.
      
      All three Diamond builds were also repeated from the consolidated layout. The
      licensed integration check passed JEDEC programming-record, pin-table and resource
      comparisons against isolated legacy projects, and a scaffolded program built in
      a separate checkout path with spaces. Fresh evidence is retained under
      ``build/validation/legacy-*/validation.json``.
      
      Standalone program layout
      ---------------------------
      
      Each program now owns ``<name>.toml``, ``<name>.vhdl``,
      ``<name>_constraints.lpf`` and ``<name>_tb.py``. HDL and LPFs were verified
      byte-for-byte against their original files when copied; normal operations use
      only the local copies. The shared runner loads the manifest's local testbench,
      and simulation provenance includes its hash.
      
      The final layout passed all 11 frontend tests and all three catalog simulations.
      A renamed copy in an unrelated temporary directory, without the old repository,
      also passed frontend tests and a strict Sphinx build. A new enable-controlled
      program was scaffolded there and its inherited local testbench passed.
      The standalone Python API treats this directory itself as the allowed input root.
      
      
      Unified container update
      --------------------------
      
      Development and CI now use ``.devcontainer/Dockerfile``. Host Make commands
      build and run that image; inside it, simulation runs directly without a Docker
      socket. The local virtual environment setup has been removed. Frontend tests,
      strict Sphinx documentation and Make command generation were checked.
      A live unified image build could not be verified in the existing environment
      because it has no Docker executable or socket. Rebuild the Dev Container to
      install the unified dependencies.
      Workspace layout
      ==================
      
      ``new_approach/`` can be copied or renamed and used independently. Within the
      current repository it is arranged as follows::
      
         uz_cpld/
         ├── MACHXO2/                 existing HDL, LPFs and released firmware
         ├── ispMACH/                 older device projects
         ├── Makefile                forwards commands into new_approach
         ├── .devcontainer/          VS Code discovery configuration
         ├── .github/workflows/      CI discovery configuration
         └── new_approach/
             ├── Makefile            build, simulation, tests and docs commands
             ├── .devcontainer/      unified Dockerfile, VS Code config and launchers
             ├── .gitignore          standalone generated-file exclusions
             ├── requirements.txt    build frontend Python dependencies
             ├── buildsystem/        model, CLI, lifecycle and vendor backend
             ├── simulation/         pytest runner, cocotb tests, dependencies
             ├── programs/           self-contained program directories
             ├── targets/            board metadata and reviewed strategy input
             ├── toolchain_tests/    frontend and licensed integration checks
             ├── docs/               this shared Sphinx project
             │   └── history/        earlier discussion and session records
             └── build/              ignored generated results
      
      Each program uses one directory with matching filenames::
      
         programs/tx30/
         ├── tx30.toml
         ├── tx30.vhdl
         ├── tx30_constraints.lpf
         └── tx30_tb.py
      
      The TOML manifest names the local HDL, LPF and cocotb testbench. Compiler and
      simulator use these same local inputs. The initial HDL/LPF files were copied
      byte-for-byte from the old projects; they are independent files with no automatic
      synchronization. There is no central constraints directory.
      
      ``make new NAME=my_adapter TEMPLATE=tx30`` creates the same four-file layout,
      including an editable testbench copied from the current ``tx30`` program.
      ``TEMPLATE`` selects an existing program; no separate template files are stored. The workspace can be
      copied or renamed without sibling directories. An optional legacy comparison
      requires an explicit ``--legacy-project /path/to/project.ldf`` argument.
      
      Generated results
      ------------------
      
      * ``build/<program>/<target>/diamond/`` contains project files, logs, firmware,
        reports and provenance.
      * ``build/simulation/<program>/`` contains traces, test logs and run metadata;
        ``build/simulation/junit.xml`` contains the pytest summary.
      * ``build/validation/`` retains licensed legacy-comparison evidence.
      * ``docs/_build/html/`` contains the generated documentation site.
      
      Local outputs produced before consolidation are preserved under
      ``build/history/pre-consolidation/`` when present. Their embedded paths describe
      the old layout; regenerate projects and outputs with the current commands.
      This archive is local evidence, not a source dependency.
      Environment setup
      ===================
      
      One Dockerfile, ``.devcontainer/Dockerfile``, provides the development and CI
      environment: Diamond runtime dependencies, GHDL, Python packages and Sphinx.
      Diamond itself still requires a mounted vendor installation and license.
      
      Simulation, tests and documentation
      -------------------------------------
      
      Install Docker Engine on the host. No host Python environment or GHDL install
      is needed for simulation. From the standalone workspace::
      
         make sim
         make test-container
         make docs-container
      
      Each command builds the same cached toolchain image and runs its task inside
      it. For CI or a full local check, ``make test-container docs-container sim``
      builds the image once for that Make invocation. Python dependencies and GHDL are
      installed in the image; no workspace virtual environment is created or selected.
      Open ``docs/_build/html/index.html`` after the documentation command.
      
      ``make test`` and ``make docs`` remain direct entry points for environments that
      already provide their tools, such as the Unified Dev Container. CI uses the
      container commands above.
      
      Unified Dev Container
      -----------------------
      
      Install Docker Engine and VS Code's Dev Containers extension on native Linux.
      From the standalone ``new_approach/`` directory, before launching VS Code::
      
         export DIAMOND_HOST_ROOT="$HOME/lscc/diamond/3.14"
         code .
      
      Choose **Dev Containers: Reopen in Container**. The installation root is the
      parent of ``bin``, not ``bin/lin64``. If VS Code was already running without the
      variable, exit it fully and relaunch. The daemon must have access to that host
      path and the checkout.
      
      ``.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`` points to
      ``.devcontainer/Dockerfile`` with the standalone workspace as build context.
      The root repository configuration uses this same Dockerfile. The image provides
      all build, simulation and documentation dependencies, and the configuration mounts
      Diamond read-only at ``/opt/diamond``. No license files are copied into the image.
      After container recipe changes use **Rebuild Container**, or **Rebuild and Reopen
      in Container**; reopening alone may reuse the existing image. The repository bind
      mount persists, while unmounted container files and manually installed packages
      may be lost on rebuild. For temporary Ubuntu packages run ``sudo apt-get update``
      before ``sudo apt-get install``.
      
      Inside the Dev Container, ``make sim``, ``make test`` and ``make docs`` run
      directly using the installed tools. No Docker socket or nested container is
      needed. The ``test-container`` and ``docs-container`` aliases also run directly
      when the image's ``CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER=1`` marker is present.
      
      The image also includes curl, ripgrep and the standalone Codex CLI; VS Code requests
      its IDE extension. Authentication is performed inside the environment and is not
      baked into the image. ``CODEX_VERSION`` is a configurable build argument; cached
      layers do not automatically refresh its ``latest`` default.
      
      From the standalone workspace, direct container use is::
      
         docker build -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile -t uz-cpld-toolchain .
         docker run --rm --network=host \
           --mount "type=bind,source=$DIAMOND_HOST_ROOT,target=/opt/diamond,readonly" \
           --mount "type=bind,source=$PWD,target=/work" \
           uz-cpld-toolchain make build PROGRAM=tx30
      
      The default user is UID/GID 1000; VS Code adjusts it to the host user. Direct
      Docker users can set ``USER_UID`` and ``USER_GID`` at image build time. For rootless
      Podman, use the same recipe and ``--userns=keep-id`` on run commands. To use Podman
      with VS Code, configure ``dev.containers.dockerPath`` and add that Podman-specific
      run argument. The earlier CLI validation used Podman 3.4.2; VS Code attachment was
      not validated by that check.
      
      Launchers and licensing
      ------------------------
      
      .. list-table:: Runtime configuration
         :header-rows: 1
      
         * - Variable
           - Purpose
         * - ``DIAMOND_HOST_ROOT``
           - Host installation directory used by the Dev Container mount.
         * - ``DIAMOND_ROOT``
           - Runtime installation root; defaults to ``/opt/diamond``.
         * - ``DIAMOND_CLI`` / ``DIAMOND_GUI``
           - Optional executable paths, not shell commands.
         * - ``LM_LICENSE_FILE``
           - Optional additional license file or ``port@server``.
      
      The vendor ``diamondc`` wrapper configures Tcl/shared libraries and prepends its
      installation's ``license/license.dat``. An extra license file needs a read-only
      mount and its container path. Native Linux host networking exposes host interfaces
      for the existing host-bound license; it is not a portable license guarantee or
      Docker Desktop networking configuration. Do not edit signed licenses or change
      host MAC addresses. Investigate vendor host-ID detection or authorized rehosting
      if licensing fails. Floating-license setups can use ``LM_LICENSE_FILE`` and need
      not inherently use host networking.
      
      Run ``check-diamond`` for Tcl startup and ``check-diamond --synthesis`` for the
      one-gate LSE smoke test. The smoke test does not route or export firmware.
      ``make doctor`` validates the catalog and startup; ``make build-all`` exercises
      full exports. For GUI work set ``DIAMOND_ROOT`` to the native host installation
      and run ``make gui PROGRAM=tx30`` with a display; the container does not forward
      a desktop.
      
      Shared image and CI
      -------------------------
      
      From ``new_approach/``::
      
         make sim
         make sim PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable
         make sim WAVE_FORMAT=fst
      
      On the host, ``make sim`` first builds ``.devcontainer/Dockerfile`` using
      Docker's layer cache, then runs the selected program testbench in a disposable
      container. Inside the Dev Container it runs the testbench directly.
      The workspace is bind-mounted at ``/work``; logs and waveforms persist under
      ``build/simulation/``. The container runs with the caller's UID/GID. Its internal
      ``_sim`` entry point invokes pytest directly, avoiding recursive container starts.
      ``sim-container`` is an alias for ``sim``; ``sim-image`` only builds the image.
      
      The image pins the Linux amd64 GHDL 4.1.0 archive by checksum and pins simulator
      Python dependencies in ``simulation/requirements.txt``. Sphinx, Tcl test support
      and GTKWave are also installed in the image. Dependency downloads occur during
      image builds, never in the workspace.
      
      ``CONTAINER_ENGINE`` defaults to ``docker`` and can select ``podman`` when running
      on a suitably configured host. ``SIM_IMAGE`` overrides the image tag, whose
      default is ``uz-cpld-toolchain``. The command requires a reachable container daemon;
      installing a CLI alone does not provide one. ``SIM_WORKSPACE`` overrides the host bind source when needed.
      
      The GitHub Actions workflow runs ``make -C new_approach test-container
      docs-container sim`` and uploads simulation evidence and the documentation site.
      It uses the same image and Make targets as local development.
      
      The mounted vendor installation, OS package updates and unpinned base image tags
      remain external inputs. See :doc:`validation` for what has actually been tested.
      Quickstart
      ============
      
      All tooling and program inputs live in the standalone ``new_approach/`` directory.
      It can be copied or renamed without the old repository. Run the following from the repository
      root after choosing an environment in :doc:`environments`::
      
         cd new_approach
         make list
         make check PROGRAM=tx30
         make test-container
         make sim PROGRAM=tx30
         make build PROGRAM=tx30
         make docs-container
      
      ``make sim`` needs Docker; GHDL and Python dependencies are installed in the image. ``make build``
      needs Diamond and a valid license. Neither is needed for manifest checks;
      Sphinx builds API documentation without running either toolchain.
      
      .. list-table:: Choose a task
         :header-rows: 1
         :widths: 30 35 35
      
         * - Task
           - Command
           - Guide
         * - Author a new adapter
           - ``make new NAME=my_adapter TEMPLATE=tx30``
           - :doc:`builds`
         * - Generate firmware
           - ``make build PROGRAM=tx30``
           - :doc:`builds`
         * - Inspect a native GUI project
           - ``make gui PROGRAM=tx30``
           - :doc:`builds`
         * - Test routing behavior
           - ``make sim``
           - :doc:`simulation`
         * - Run frontend regressions
           - ``make test-container``
           - :doc:`validation`
         * - Read generated documentation
           - ``make docs-container``
           - ``docs/_build/html/index.html``
      
      The root Makefile forwards these same targets, so existing ``make`` commands
      still work from the repository root. File paths in workflow examples are
      relative to ``new_approach/`` unless explicitly stated otherwise.
      
      A typical development cycle is to create/edit a program, validate its manifest,
      adapt the generated program-local testbench, run simulation, then generate
      firmware. New programs inherit the source program's behavior contract and can be
      selected immediately with ``make sim PROGRAM=<name>``. Update that contract
      when changing the program's behavior.
      
      The two workflows produce different evidence: RTL simulation checks logical
      behavior, while Diamond implements that logic on the device. See :doc:`validation`
      for electrical, timing, GUI and hardware acceptance limits.
      .DEFAULT_GOAL := build
      PYTHON ?= python3
      TARGET ?= uz_dslot_xo2
      TEMPLATE ?= tx30
      # Quote values as single shell arguments, including embedded apostrophes.
      quote = '$(subst ','"'"',$(1))'
      ARGS = --target $(call quote,$(TARGET)) $(if $(PROGRAM),--program $(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) $(if $(TOOLCHAIN),--toolchain $(call quote,$(TOOLCHAIN)))
      .PHONY: build list doctor new check project gui build-all clean test docs sim sim-image sim-container test-container docs-container _sim
      build list doctor check project gui build-all:
      	$(PYTHON) -m buildsystem $@ $(ARGS)
      new:
      	$(PYTHON) -m buildsystem new $(ARGS) --name $(call quote,$(NAME)) --template $(call quote,$(TEMPLATE))
      clean:
      	$(PYTHON) -m buildsystem clean $(ARGS) $(if $(filter 1,$(DISCARD_PROJECT_CHANGES)),--discard-project-changes)
      test:
      	$(PYTHON) -m unittest discover -s toolchain_tests -v
      CONTAINER_ENGINE ?= docker
      SIM_IMAGE ?= uz-cpld-toolchain
      # Bind source for commands run from the host.
      SIM_WORKSPACE ?= $(CURDIR)
      SEED ?= 1
      WAVE_FORMAT ?= ghw
      CONTAINER_RUN = $(CONTAINER_ENGINE) run --rm --user "$$(id -u):$$(id -g)" --mount $(call quote,type=bind$(comma)source=$(SIM_WORKSPACE)$(comma)target=/work) -w /work $(call quote,$(SIM_IMAGE))
      comma := ,
      sim-image:
      	@command -v $(CONTAINER_ENGINE) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Container engine missing. Install Docker on the host or reopen in the unified Dev Container." >&2; exit 1; }
      	$(CONTAINER_ENGINE) build -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile -t $(call quote,$(SIM_IMAGE)) .
      ifeq ($(CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER),1)
      sim: _sim
      test-container: test
      docs-container: docs
      else
      sim: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make _sim $(if $(PROGRAM),PROGRAM=$(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) SEED=$(call quote,$(SEED)) WAVE_FORMAT=$(call quote,$(WAVE_FORMAT))
      test-container: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make test
      docs-container: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make docs
      endif
      # Compatibility alias.
      sim-container: sim
      # Image-internal entry point. Never creates or selects a host virtual environment.
      _sim:
      	@test "$(CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER)" = "1" || { echo "Use 'make sim' to run in the simulation container." >&2; exit 1; }
      	python3 -m pytest simulation/test_simulation.py -v --junitxml=build/simulation/junit.xml $(if $(PROGRAM),--program $(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) --seed $(call quote,$(SEED)) --wave-format $(call quote,$(WAVE_FORMAT))
      docs:
      	$(PYTHON) -m sphinx -W --keep-going -b html docs docs/_build/html
      """Load and validate explicit program and board manifests without running tools."""
      from dataclasses import dataclass
      from pathlib import Path
      import re
      try:
          import tomllib
      except ModuleNotFoundError:
          import tomli as tomllib
      
      
      class BuildError(Exception):
          """An actionable configuration or build failure."""
      
      
      def identifier(value: str) -> str:
          """Validate a filesystem-safe program, target, or backend name."""
          if not isinstance(value, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*", value):
              raise BuildError(f"Invalid name: {value!r}; use lowercase letters, digits and underscores")
          return value
      
      
      def read_toml(path: Path) -> dict:
          """Read a manifest, reporting parse and filesystem errors consistently."""
          try:
              with path.open('rb') as stream:
                  return tomllib.load(stream)
          except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
              raise BuildError(f"{path}: {exc}") from exc
      
      
      def keys(data: dict, allowed: set, required: set, label: str):
          """Reject unknown fields and missing required fields."""
          if not isinstance(data, dict):
              raise BuildError(f"{label}: expected a table")
          if set(data) - allowed or required - set(data):
              raise BuildError(f"{label}: unknown fields {sorted(set(data)-allowed)}, missing fields {sorted(required-set(data))}")
      
      
      def input_path(root: Path, base: Path, value: str) -> Path:
          """Resolve an existing input within the checkout, including symlink checks."""
          if not isinstance(value, str) or Path(value).is_absolute():
              raise BuildError(f"Input path must be relative: {value!r}")
          path = (base / value).resolve()
          if not path.is_relative_to(root.resolve()) or not path.is_file():
              raise BuildError(f"Missing input or input outside checkout: {path}")
          return path
      
      
      def strings(value, label):
          """Validate a list of distinct strings."""
          if not isinstance(value, list) or any(not isinstance(v, str) for v in value) or len(set(value)) != len(value):
              raise BuildError(f"{label}: expected a list of unique strings")
          return value
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True)
      class Source:
          """An ordered VHDL input and its compilation library."""
          path: Path
          library: str
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True)
      class Build:
          """Validated inputs for one program, board target and backend."""
          root: Path
          name: str
          target: str
          backend: str
          top: str
          standard: str
          sources: tuple[Source, ...]
          constraint: Path
          device: str
          strategy: Path
          options: dict
          manifests: tuple[Path, ...]
          expected_version: str
          testbench: Path
      
          @property
          def directory(self) -> Path:
              """Generated output location; never an authored source directory."""
              return self.root / 'build' / self.name / self.target / self.backend
      
          @property
          def inputs(self) -> tuple[Path, ...]:
              """All authored inputs included in provenance."""
              return tuple(s.path for s in self.sources) + (self.constraint, self.strategy, self.testbench) + self.manifests
      
      
      def catalog(root: Path) -> list[str]:
          """Return the explicitly supported catalog, excluding uncatalogued programs and archives."""
          data = read_toml(root / 'programs/catalog.toml')
          keys(data, {'programs'}, {'programs'}, 'catalog')
          return [identifier(n) for n in strings(data['programs'], 'catalog.programs')]
      
      
      def load_build(root: Path, name: str, target: str = 'uz_dslot_xo2', backend: str | None = None) -> Build:
          """Validate manifests and return a build model; no vendor tools are needed."""
          root = root.resolve()
          name, target = identifier(name), identifier(target)
          pm = input_path(root, root, f'programs/{name}/{name}.toml')
          tm = input_path(root, root, f'targets/{target}/target.toml')
          p, t = read_toml(pm), read_toml(tm)
          pf = {'name', 'top', 'standard', 'sources', 'targets', 'constraints', 'testbench'}
          tf = {'name', 'device', 'backend', 'diamond'}
          keys(p, pf, pf, str(pm)); keys(t, tf, tf, str(tm))
          if p['name'] != name or t['name'] != target:
              raise BuildError('Manifest name must match its directory')
          if target not in strings(p['targets'], 'targets'):
              raise BuildError(f'{name} does not support {target}')
          backend = identifier(backend or t['backend'])
          if backend != 'diamond' or t['backend'] != 'diamond':
              raise BuildError(f'Unimplemented backend: {backend}')
          if p['standard'] not in ('1993', '2008'):
              raise BuildError('VHDL standard must be "1993" or "2008"')
          hdl_id = r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(?:_[A-Za-z0-9]+)*'
          if not isinstance(p['top'], str) or not re.fullmatch(hdl_id, p['top']):
              raise BuildError('Invalid VHDL top entity')
          if not isinstance(p['sources'], list) or not p['sources']:
              raise BuildError('sources must be a nonempty ordered list')
          sources = []
          for s in p['sources']:
              keys(s, {'path', 'library'}, {'path', 'library'}, 'source')
              if not isinstance(s['library'], str) or not re.fullmatch(hdl_id, s['library']):
                  raise BuildError('Invalid VHDL library')
              sources.append(Source(input_path(root, pm.parent, s['path']), s['library']))
          if len({s.path for s in sources}) != len(sources):
              raise BuildError('Duplicate source path')
          constraints = strings(p['constraints'], 'constraints')
          if len(constraints) != 1:
              raise BuildError('First version requires exactly one authored LPF; composition is not implemented')
          constraint = input_path(root, pm.parent, constraints[0])
          if constraint.suffix.lower() != '.lpf':
              raise BuildError('Constraint must be an LPF')
          testbench = input_path(root, pm.parent, p['testbench'])
          if testbench != pm.parent / f'{name}_tb.py':
              raise BuildError('Testbench must be named <program>_tb.py in the program directory')
          d = t['diamond']
          keys(d, {'strategy', 'version', 'options'}, {'strategy', 'version', 'options'}, 'diamond')
          if not isinstance(d['options'], dict) or any(not isinstance(v, str) for v in d['options'].values()):
              raise BuildError('Diamond options must be a table of string values')
          if any(not re.fullmatch(r'[a-z][a-z0-9_]*', k) for k in d['options']):
              raise BuildError('Invalid Diamond strategy option name')
          if 'lse_vhdl2008' in d['options']:
              raise BuildError('Use program.standard instead of lse_vhdl2008')
          if t['device'] != 'LCMXO2-2000HC-4TG100C':
              raise BuildError('Only LCMXO2-2000HC-4TG100C is validated by this backend')
          if not isinstance(d['version'], str) or not d['version']:
              raise BuildError('diamond.version must specify the required tool version')
          return Build(root, name, target, backend, p['top'], p['standard'], tuple(sources), constraint,
                       t['device'], input_path(root, tm.parent, d['strategy']), d['options'], (pm, tm), d['version'], testbench)
      """Command-line interface for manifests, scaffolding, projects and builds."""
      import argparse
      from pathlib import Path
      import sys
      import tempfile
      from .model import BuildError, catalog, load_build
      from . import workflow
      from .backends.diamond import launcher, run, wrap
      
      
      def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
          """Execute a command and return a shell-compatible status code."""
          parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
          parser.add_argument('command', choices=['list', 'doctor', 'new', 'check', 'project', 'build', 'gui', 'build-all', 'clean'])
          parser.add_argument('--root', type=Path, default=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1])
          parser.add_argument('--program')
          parser.add_argument('--target', default='uz_dslot_xo2')
          parser.add_argument('--toolchain')
          parser.add_argument('--name')
          parser.add_argument('--template', default='tx30', help='Existing program to clone (default: tx30)')
          parser.add_argument('--discard-project-changes', action='store_true')
          args = parser.parse_args(argv)
          root = args.root.resolve()
          try:
              if args.discard_project_changes and args.command != 'clean':
                  raise BuildError('--discard-project-changes is only valid for clean')
              if args.command == 'list':
                  for name in catalog(root):
                      build = load_build(root, name, args.target, args.toolchain)
                      print(f'{name}\t{build.target}\t{build.backend}')
              elif args.command == 'doctor':
                  print(f'Python: {sys.version.split()[0]}\nDiamond: {launcher()}')
                  for name in catalog(root):
                      load_build(root, name, args.target, args.toolchain)
                  with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='cpld-doctor-') as tmp:
                      script = Path(tmp) / 'doctor.tcl'
                      script.write_text(wrap(['if {[llength [info commands prj_project]] == 0} {error "Project Tcl unavailable"}', 'puts "Diamond project Tcl available"']))
                      print(run(script, Path(tmp) / 'doctor.log').strip())
                  print('Catalog and Tcl startup passed; run build to validate synthesis and exports.')
              elif args.command == 'new':
                  if not args.name:
                      raise BuildError('new requires --name (Make: NAME=...)')
                  print(workflow.scaffold(root, args.name, args.template, args.target))
              elif args.command == 'build-all':
                  failed = []
                  for name in catalog(root):
                      try:
                          print(workflow.build_program(load_build(root, name, args.target, args.toolchain)))
                      except (BuildError, OSError, ValueError) as exc:
                          failed.append(name); print(f'{name}: {exc}', file=sys.stderr)
                  if failed:
                      raise BuildError('Failed programs: ' + ', '.join(failed))
              else:
                  if not args.program:
                      raise BuildError(f'{args.command} requires --program (Make: PROGRAM=...)')
                  build = load_build(root, args.program, args.target, args.toolchain)
                  if args.command == 'check':
                      print(f'{build.name}: manifest and inputs valid')
                  elif args.command == 'clean':
                      workflow.clean(build, args.discard_project_changes)
                  else:
                      action = workflow.build_program if args.command == 'build' else getattr(workflow, args.command)
                      result = action(build)
                      if result:
                          print(result)
              return 0
          except (BuildError, OSError, ValueError) as exc:
              print(f'error: {exc}', file=sys.stderr)
              return 1
      
      
      if __name__ == '__main__':
          raise SystemExit(main())
      """Generate and execute Diamond Tcl using the vendor environment wrapper."""
      import os
      from pathlib import Path
      import shutil
      import subprocess
      import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
      from ..model import Build, BuildError
      
      
      def tcl(value: str) -> str:
          """Quote one Tcl word without allowing variable or command substitution."""
          return '"' + str(value).replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"').replace('$', '\\$').replace('[', '\\[').replace(']', '\\]').replace('\n', '\\n').replace('\r', '\\r') + '"'
      
      
      def launcher(gui: bool = False) -> Path:
          """Find a configurable vendor launcher; overrides are executable paths."""
          override = os.environ.get('DIAMOND_GUI' if gui else 'DIAMOND_CLI')
          root = Path(os.environ.get('DIAMOND_ROOT', '/opt/diamond'))
          candidate = override or str(root / 'bin/lin64' / ('diamond' if gui else 'diamondc'))
          found = shutil.which(candidate)
          if not found:
              raise BuildError(f'Diamond launcher unavailable: {candidate}; set DIAMOND_ROOT or DIAMOND_CLI/DIAMOND_GUI')
          return Path(found).resolve()
      
      
      def run(script: Path, log: Path) -> str:
          """Run Tcl without a display or stdin, preserving output even on failure."""
          env = dict(os.environ)
          env.pop('DISPLAY', None); env.pop('WAYLAND_DISPLAY', None)
          with log.open('w') as stream:
              result = subprocess.run([str(launcher()), script.name], cwd=script.parent,
                                      env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=stream, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
          output = log.read_text(errors='replace')
          if result.returncode:
              raise BuildError(f'Diamond exited {result.returncode}; see {log}\n{output[-1800:]}')
          return output
      
      
      class DiamondBackend:
          """Prepare relocatable projects and request both firmware export tasks."""
      
          def prepare(self, build: Build, project: Path, log: Path):
              """Generate a project whose HDL and LPF references point to authored inputs."""
              project.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
              shutil.copy2(build.strategy, project / 'baseline.sty')
              relative = lambda p: tcl(os.path.relpath(p, project))
              lines = [f'prj_project new -name firmware -impl impl -impl_dir impl -dev {tcl(build.device)} -lpf {relative(build.constraint)}',
                       'prj_syn set lse',
                       'prj_strgy import -name baseline -file baseline.sty', 'prj_strgy set baseline']
              for source in build.sources:
                  lines.append(f'prj_src add -format VHDL -work {tcl(source.library)} {relative(source.path)}')
              options = dict(build.options, lse_vhdl2008='True' if build.standard == '2008' else 'False')
              for key, value in sorted(options.items()):
                  lines.append(f'prj_strgy set_value {tcl(key + "=" + value)}')
              lines += ['prj_project save', 'prj_project close']
              script = project / 'prepare.tcl'
              script.write_text(wrap(lines))
              run(script, log)
              if not (project / 'firmware.ldf').is_file():
                  raise BuildError(f'Diamond did not create a project; see {log}')
              # Diamond exposes def_top as internal-only in Tcl. Store it in its LDF schema.
              ldf = project / 'firmware.ldf'
              tree = ET.parse(ldf)
              implementation = tree.getroot().find('Implementation')
              opts = implementation.find('Options')
              if opts is None:
                  opts = ET.SubElement(implementation, 'Options')
              opts.set('def_top', build.top)
              tree.write(ldf, encoding='UTF-8', xml_declaration=True)
      
          def build(self, project: Path, log: Path) -> str:
              """Run synthesis through PAR, timing reporting and both export tasks."""
              lines = ['prj_project open firmware.ldf', 'prj_run Synthesis -impl impl',
                       'prj_run Translate -impl impl', 'prj_run Map -impl impl',
                       'prj_run PAR -impl impl', 'prj_run PAR -impl impl -task PARTrace',
                       'prj_run Export -impl impl -task Bitgen',
                       'prj_run Export -impl impl -task Jedecgen', 'prj_project close']
              script = project / 'build.tcl'
              script.write_text(wrap(lines))
              return run(script, log)
      
      
      def wrap(lines: list[str]) -> str:
          """Turn Tcl errors into a nonzero process exit."""
          return 'if {[catch {\n' + '\n'.join(lines) + '\n} message]} {\nputs stderr $message\nexit 1\n}\nexit 0\n'
