      ``check`` validates inputs without Diamond. ``doctor`` also checks Tcl startup;
      it does not establish synthesis or export success. ``build-all`` processes the
      explicit catalog and returns failure if any catalog entry fails.
      
      Outputs are under ``build/<program>/<target>/<backend>/``:
      
      * ``project/``: generated LDF, strategy, Tcl, and tool intermediates.
      * ``logs/``: timestamped preparation/build logs, retained across builds.
      * ``artifacts/``: fresh ``firmware.jed``, ``firmware.bit``, reports and ``build.json``.
      * ``configuration.json``: hashes used to detect edited generated settings.
      * ``status.json``: status of the last build that passed the initial guards.
      
      Once a build passes the lock and generated-configuration guards, it removes
      previous artifacts; failures during preparation or compilation leave no current
      artifacts and preserve available logs. An earlier rejection, such as invalid
      inputs, an active lock or edited generated settings, leaves previous outputs
      and status untouched. ``project`` regenerates project files without refreshing
      firmware or build status; consult ``build.json`` for the inputs of an export. Build operations
      never program a device. Existing released firmware in legacy directories is
      preserved.
      
      Create a program
      ----------------
      
      Clone an existing program and edit the resulting files::
      
         make new NAME=my_adapter TEMPLATE=tx30
         # Edit my_adapter.vhdl, my_adapter_constraints.lpf and my_adapter_tb.py
         # inside programs/my_adapter/.
         make check PROGRAM=my_adapter
         make sim PROGRAM=my_adapter
         make build PROGRAM=my_adapter
      
      ``TEMPLATE`` names an existing program directory, defaulting to ``tx30``.
      A program supporting the selected target can be the source, including one you
      created yourself. The
      command copies its current authored files, renames the four primary files, and
      updates manifest references while preserving source order, libraries, target
      support, HDL entity names and testbench behavior. Additional local files are
      copied too; Python caches are excluded. There is no separate ``templates/`` tree.
      The primary HDL must be named ``<template>.vhdl`` and listed in its manifest.
      Inputs outside the source program directory must be localized before cloning;
      symlinks within that directory are rejected.
      The clone is independent: future edits to the original do not update it.
      The generated manifest is ``programs/<name>/<name>.toml``. Creation refuses an
      existing destination. New programs are not automatically added to ``build-all``;
      review their behavior and constraints before adding them to
      ``programs/catalog.toml``.
      
      The ``tx26_w_enable`` program forwards channels 0–25 when FPGA channels 26–29 are
      0, 0, 1, 1 and ``reqsafestate`` is low. Its declared outputs 26–29 remain
      undriven, matching the legacy source. Review the reports when cloning this program.
      
      The build frontend commands are also available through Python, for example::
      
         python3 -m buildsystem build --program tx30 --target uz_dslot_xo2
         python3 -m buildsystem --help
      
      The Python CLI provides ``list``, ``doctor``, ``new``, ``check``, ``project``,
      ``build``, ``gui``, ``build-all`` and ``clean``. Simulation, tooling tests,
      documentation and container commands are separate Make targets. ``make`` without
      a target defaults to ``build`` and requires ``PROGRAM``. ``TARGET`` defaults to
      ``uz_dslot_xo2``; ``TOOLCHAIN`` selects the backend, currently only ``diamond``.
      
      GUI workflow
      ------------
      
      On a Linux host with a display and a native Diamond installation::
      
         make project PROGRAM=tx30
         make gui PROGRAM=tx30
      
      Generated projects reference authored HDL and LPF files using relative paths.
      Edits to those authored files persist. Verify the destination when saving from
      Spreadsheet View: an exported/generated LPF does not replace the authored LPF.
      Useful GUI changes to project membership or strategy must be transferred manually
      into manifests or the target strategy baseline.
      
      ``gui`` opens an existing project without regenerating it, preserving experiments.
      ``project`` and ``build`` regenerate settings and reject externally modified
      LDF/strategy/Tcl files. After transferring useful changes, discard generated work::
      # CPLD build and simulation workspace
      
      This directory contains the headless Diamond build system and GHDL/cocotb
      simulator, sharing program manifests and one Sphinx documentation project.
      It is standalone: copy or rename this directory, install the documented tools,
      and run its Makefile without the old repository.
      
      ```sh
      cd new_approach  # from the repository root
      make list
      make build PROGRAM=tx30
      make sim
      make test-container
      make docs-container
      ```
      
      Start with the [shared quickstart](docs/getting-started.rst) and
      [environment setup](docs/environments.rst). See the [layout](docs/layout.rst),
      [build guide](docs/builds.rst), [simulation guide](docs/simulation.rst),
      [configuration](docs/configuration.rst), and [Python API](docs/api.rst).
      `make docs-container` creates `docs/_build/html/index.html`.
      
      - `buildsystem/`: Python CLI, validated model, workflow and Diamond backend.
      - `simulation/`: shared pytest/GHDL runner.
      - `programs/<name>/`: `<name>.toml`, `<name>.vhdl`,
        `<name>_constraints.lpf`, and `<name>_tb.py` (cocotb).
      - `targets/`: board configuration. Existing programs serve as cloning sources.
      - `toolchain_tests/`: build-tool self-tests and an optional licensed Diamond integration check.
      - `.devcontainer/`: unified Dockerfile, VS Code configuration and Diamond launchers.
      - `docs/`: unified current documentation; `docs/history/` holds earlier records.
      - `build/`: ignored firmware, reports, simulation traces and validation evidence.

      	$(PYTHON) -m buildsystem clean $(ARGS) $(if $(filter 1,$(DISCARD_PROJECT_CHANGES)),--discard-project-changes)
      test:
      	$(PYTHON) -m unittest discover -s toolchain_tests -v
      CONTAINER_ENGINE ?= docker
      SIM_IMAGE ?= uz-cpld-toolchain
      # Bind source for commands run from the host.
      SIM_WORKSPACE ?= $(CURDIR)
      SEED ?= 1
      WAVE_FORMAT ?= ghw
      CONTAINER_RUN = $(CONTAINER_ENGINE) run --rm --user "$$(id -u):$$(id -g)" --mount $(call quote,type=bind$(comma)source=$(SIM_WORKSPACE)$(comma)target=/work) -w /work $(call quote,$(SIM_IMAGE))
      comma := ,
      sim-image:
      	@command -v $(CONTAINER_ENGINE) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Container engine missing. Install Docker on the host or reopen in the unified Dev Container." >&2; exit 1; }
      	$(CONTAINER_ENGINE) build -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile -t $(call quote,$(SIM_IMAGE)) .
      ifeq ($(CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER),1)
      sim: _sim
      test-container: test
      docs-container: docs
      else
      sim: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make _sim $(if $(PROGRAM),PROGRAM=$(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) SEED=$(call quote,$(SEED)) WAVE_FORMAT=$(call quote,$(WAVE_FORMAT))
      test-container: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make test
      docs-container: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make docs
      endif
      # Compatibility alias.
      sim-container: sim
      # Image-internal entry point. Never creates or selects a host virtual environment.
      _sim:
      	@test "$(CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER)" = "1" || { echo "Use 'make sim' to run in the simulation container." >&2; exit 1; }
      	python3 -m pytest simulation/test_simulation.py -v --junitxml=build/simulation/junit.xml $(if $(PROGRAM),--program $(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) --seed $(call quote,$(SEED)) --wave-format $(call quote,$(WAVE_FORMAT))
      docs:
      	$(PYTHON) -m sphinx -W --keep-going -b html docs docs/_build/html
      Environment setup
      ===================
      
      One Dockerfile, ``.devcontainer/Dockerfile``, provides the development and CI
      environment: Diamond runtime dependencies, GHDL, Python packages and Sphinx.
      Diamond itself still requires a mounted vendor installation and license.
      
      Simulation, tests and documentation
      -------------------------------------
      
      Install Docker Engine on the host. No host Python environment or GHDL install
      is needed for simulation. From the standalone workspace::
      
         make sim
         make test-container
         make docs-container
      
      Each command builds the same cached toolchain image and runs its task inside
      it. For CI or a full local check, ``make test-container docs-container sim``
      builds the image once for that Make invocation. Python dependencies and GHDL are
      installed in the image; no workspace virtual environment is created or selected.
      Open ``docs/_build/html/index.html`` after the documentation command.
      
      ``make test`` and ``make docs`` remain direct entry points for environments that
      already provide their tools, such as the Unified Dev Container. The frontend
      requires Python 3.10 or newer; Python 3.10 also needs ``tomli``. For a native
      Python setup, install ``requirements.txt`` for the frontend and
      ``docs/requirements.txt`` for documentation. Frontend tests also require
      ``tkinter`` (Ubuntu package ``python3-tk``) for Tcl quoting checks. CI uses the
      container commands above. Firmware commands such as ``make build`` always run
      in the calling environment, so run them inside the Dev Container or provide a
      native Diamond installation.
      
      Unified Dev Container
      -----------------------
      
      Install Docker Engine and VS Code's Dev Containers extension on native Linux.
      From the standalone ``new_approach/`` directory, before launching VS Code::
      
         export DIAMOND_HOST_ROOT="$HOME/lscc/diamond/3.14"
         code .
      
      Choose **Dev Containers: Reopen in Container**. The installation root is the
      parent of ``bin``, not ``bin/lin64``. If VS Code was already running without the
      variable, exit it fully and relaunch. The daemon must have access to that host
      path and the checkout.
      
      ``.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`` points to
      ``.devcontainer/Dockerfile`` with the standalone workspace as build context.
      The root repository configuration uses this same Dockerfile. The image provides
      all build, simulation and documentation dependencies, and the configuration mounts
      Diamond read-only at ``/opt/diamond``. No license files are copied into the image.
      After container recipe changes use **Rebuild Container**, or **Rebuild and Reopen
      in Container**; reopening alone may reuse the existing image. The repository bind
      mount persists, while unmounted container files and manually installed packages
      may be lost on rebuild. For temporary Ubuntu packages run ``sudo apt-get update``
      before ``sudo apt-get install``.
      
      Inside the Dev Container, ``make sim``, ``make test`` and ``make docs`` run
      directly using the installed tools. No Docker socket or nested container is
      needed. The ``test-container`` and ``docs-container`` aliases also run directly
      when the image's ``CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER=1`` marker is present.
      
      The image also includes curl, ripgrep and the standalone Codex CLI; VS Code requests
      its IDE extension. Authentication is performed inside the environment and is not
      baked into the image. ``CODEX_VERSION`` is a configurable build argument; cached
      layers do not automatically refresh its ``latest`` default.
      
      From the standalone workspace, direct container use is::
      
         docker build -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile -t uz-cpld-toolchain .
         docker run --rm --network=host \
           --mount "type=bind,source=$DIAMOND_HOST_ROOT,target=/opt/diamond,readonly" \
           --mount "type=bind,source=$PWD,target=/work" \
           uz-cpld-toolchain make build PROGRAM=tx30
      
      The default user is UID/GID 1000; VS Code adjusts it to the host user. Direct
      Docker users can set ``USER_UID`` and ``USER_GID`` at image build time. For rootless
      Podman, use the same recipe and ``--userns=keep-id`` on run commands. To use Podman
      with VS Code, configure ``dev.containers.dockerPath`` and add that Podman-specific
      run argument. The earlier CLI validation used Podman 3.4.2; VS Code attachment was
      not validated by that check.
      
      Launchers and licensing
      ------------------------
      
      .. list-table:: Runtime configuration
         :header-rows: 1
      
         * - Variable
           - Purpose
         * - ``DIAMOND_HOST_ROOT``
           - Host installation directory used by the Dev Container mount.
         * - ``DIAMOND_ROOT``
           - Runtime installation root; defaults to ``/opt/diamond``.
         * - ``DIAMOND_CLI`` / ``DIAMOND_GUI``
           - Python frontend launcher overrides: executable paths, not shell commands.
         * - ``LM_LICENSE_FILE``
           - Optional additional license file or ``port@server``.
      
      The vendor ``diamondc`` wrapper configures Tcl/shared libraries and prepends its
      installation's ``license/license.dat``. An extra license file needs a read-only
      mount and its container path. Native Linux host networking exposes host interfaces
      for the existing host-bound license; it is not a portable license guarantee or
      Docker Desktop networking configuration. Do not edit signed licenses or change
      host MAC addresses. Investigate vendor host-ID detection or authorized rehosting
      if licensing fails. Floating-license setups can use ``LM_LICENSE_FILE`` and need
      not inherently use host networking.
      
      Run ``check-diamond`` for Tcl startup and ``check-diamond --synthesis`` for the
      one-gate LSE smoke test. Dev Container creation automatically runs the startup
      check only. These shell helpers use ``DIAMOND_ROOT`` and do not read the Python
      frontend's ``DIAMOND_CLI`` override. The smoke test does not route or export firmware.
      ``make doctor`` validates the catalog and startup; ``make build-all`` exercises
      full exports. For GUI work set ``DIAMOND_ROOT`` to the native host installation
      and run ``make gui PROGRAM=tx30`` with a display; the container does not forward
      a desktop.
      
      Shared image and CI
      -------------------------
      
      From ``new_approach/``::
      
         make sim
         make sim PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable
         make sim WAVE_FORMAT=fst
      
      On the host, ``make sim`` first builds ``.devcontainer/Dockerfile`` using
      Docker's layer cache, then runs the selected program testbench in a disposable
      container. Inside the Dev Container it runs the testbench directly.
      The workspace is bind-mounted at ``/work``; logs and waveforms persist under
      ``build/simulation/``. The container runs with the caller's UID/GID. Its internal
      ``_sim`` entry point invokes pytest directly, avoiding recursive container starts.
      ``sim-container`` is an alias for ``sim``; ``sim-image`` only builds the image.
      
      The image pins the Linux amd64 GHDL 4.1.0 archive by checksum and pins simulator
      Python dependencies in ``simulation/requirements.txt``. Sphinx, Tcl test support
      and GTKWave are installed from Ubuntu packages in the image. The Dockerfile does
      not install ``docs/requirements.txt``: its Sphinx version comes from apt, while
      that requirements file pins Sphinx 7.4.7 for a separate native Python setup. Dependency downloads occur during
      image builds, never in the workspace.
      
      ``CONTAINER_ENGINE`` defaults to ``docker`` and can select ``podman`` when running
      on a suitably configured host. ``SIM_IMAGE`` overrides the image tag, whose
      default is ``uz-cpld-toolchain``. The command requires a reachable container daemon;
      installing a CLI alone does not provide one. ``SIM_WORKSPACE`` overrides the host bind source when needed.
      
      The GitHub Actions workflow runs ``make -C new_approach test-container
      docs-container sim`` and uploads simulation evidence and the documentation site.
      It uses the same image and Make targets as local development.
      
      The mounted vendor installation, OS package updates and unpinned base image tags
      remain external inputs. See :doc:`validation` for what has actually been tested.

## Assistant

The setup works in the current container, but it is too tightly coupled to one developer’s Linux/Diamond environment. These are the main findings, ordered by impact.

1. **The Dev Container requires Diamond even for documentation or simulation.**
   Both configurations unconditionally mount `DIAMOND_HOST_ROOT` and run `check-diamond`. Without that installation, users cannot use the standard Dev Container configuration for otherwise license-free tasks. Make Diamond an optional configuration layered onto a general development environment. [Configuration](/workspaces/uz_cpld/new_approach/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json:10)

2. **Every documentation and CI image build also installs Codex and Diamond runtime dependencies.**
   A clean `make docs` on the host depends on downloading and executing the Codex installer, although documentation needs none of it. An installer outage or changing `latest` release can therefore break unrelated checks. Use a shared toolchain stage and a development stage that adds interactive tools. Docker explicitly supports reusable stages for this purpose. [Dockerfile](/workspaces/uz_cpld/new_approach/.devcontainer/Dockerfile:38), [Docker guidance](https://docs.docker.com/build/building/best-practices/)

3. **The image implicitly requires amd64 but does not enforce it.**
   The downloaded GHDL executable is x86-64, which I verified locally. An ARM host builds from its native Ubuntu image and then encounters an incompatible executable. Declare the supported platform or reject unsupported architectures early. [Dockerfile](/workspaces/uz_cpld/new_approach/.devcontainer/Dockerfile:12)

4. **The advertised Podman override is incomplete.**
   `CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman` changes the executable, but the generated command still uses Docker-style numeric UID/GID handling without `--userns=keep-id`. With default rootless mappings, this can prevent writes to the mounted checkout. Add engine-specific user mapping or configurable run arguments. [Makefile](/workspaces/uz_cpld/new_approach/Makefile:23), [Podman user-namespace documentation](https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-run.1.html)

5. **Dependency versions have two sources of truth.**
   The image installs Sphinx through apt—currently **4.3.2**—while `docs/requirements.txt` specifies **7.4.7**. The Ubuntu image, apt packages, and Codex installer also remain mutable. Consequently, the same checkout can produce different environments. Consolidate Python requirements and define an explicit image update/pinning policy. [Dockerfile](/workspaces/uz_cpld/new_approach/.devcontainer/Dockerfile:5), [Documentation requirements](/workspaces/uz_cpld/new_approach/docs/requirements.txt:2)

6. **CI skips later checks after an earlier failure.**
   Tests, documentation, and simulation run in one Make invocation without `-k`. A frontend or documentation failure prevents simulation from running; `if: always()` on artifact uploads cannot recover results that were never generated. Build the image once, then run independent checks in separate steps. [Workflow](/workspaces/uz_cpld/.github/workflows/toolchain.yml:16)

7. **`USERNAME` is configurable only halfway.**
   Account creation uses the argument, but `USER vscode`, the home-directory PATH, and `remoteUser` are hardcoded. Overriding `USERNAME` breaks the image/configuration. Either remove that argument or apply it consistently. [Dockerfile](/workspaces/uz_cpld/new_approach/.devcontainer/Dockerfile:22)

Host networking is also unconditional. It has a documented licensing purpose here, but it removes network isolation for all development tasks. It belongs with the optional Diamond configuration. [Docker networking behavior](https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/host/)

The good parts are worth retaining: the read-only Diamond mount, checksum-verified GHDL download, restricted build context, shared local/CI recipe, and execution without nested Docker inside the Dev Container.

I changed no files. Shell syntax, configuration consistency, and installed Python dependency checks passed. A fresh Docker/Podman build could not be tested because neither engine is available here.

      def jed_payload(path):
          """Compare programming records, excluding JEDEC notes and transport checksum."""
          data = path.read_text(errors='replace').split('\x02', 1)[-1].split('\x03', 1)[0]
          records = [re.sub(r'\s+', '', r) for r in data.split('*')
                  if re.match(r'^(QF|QP|F[01]|L\d|C[0-9A-F]|E[01]|G[01]|J\d|U)', r.strip())]
          if not any(r.startswith('QF') for r in records) or not any(r.startswith('L') for r in records):
              raise RuntimeError(f'Incomplete JEDEC programming records: {path}')
          return records
      
      
      def compare_reports(reference, generated):
          """Compare pin table rows and resource counts, ignoring report headers."""
          results = {}
          for ext, select in [('pad', lambda line: line.startswith('|')),
                              ('mrp', lambda line: 'out of' in line or 'used :' in line)]:
              left = [line.strip() for line in reference.with_suffix('.' + ext).read_text().splitlines() if select(line)]
              right = [line.strip() for line in generated.with_suffix('.' + ext).read_text().splitlines() if select(line)]
              results[ext + '_matches'] = bool(left) and left == right
          return results
      
      
      def main():
          parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
          parser.add_argument('--legacy-project', type=Path,
                              help='Optional external LDF for legacy comparison; not required')
          args = parser.parse_args()
          results = {}
          # Keep all evidence beneath ignored build/validation; unique directory per run.
          output = ROOT / 'build/validation'; output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
          stage = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='integration-', dir=output))
          for name in catalog(ROOT) if args.legacy_project else []:
              dest = stage / name; dest.mkdir()
              legacy = args.legacy_project.resolve().parent
              tree = ET.parse(args.legacy_project)
              project = tree.getroot(); project.set('default_implementation', name)
              for impl in list(project.findall('Implementation')):
                  if impl.get('title') != name:
                      project.remove(impl)
                  else:
                      for source in impl.findall('Source'):
                          original = legacy / source.get('name')
                          source.set('name', str(original))
              for strategy in project.findall('Strategy'):
                  shutil.copy2(legacy / strategy.get('file'), dest / strategy.get('file'))
              tree.write(dest / 'uz_d_slots.ldf', encoding='UTF-8', xml_declaration=True)
              script = dest / 'legacy.tcl'
              script.write_text(wrap(['prj_project open uz_d_slots.ldf',
                  f'prj_run Export -impl {tcl(name)} -task Bitgen',
                  f'prj_run Export -impl {tcl(name)} -task Jedecgen',
                  f'prj_run PAR -impl {tcl(name)} -task PARTrace', 'prj_project close']))
              run(script, dest / 'legacy.log')
              reference = dest / name / f'uz_d_slots_{name}.jed'
              generated = load_build(ROOT, name).directory / 'artifacts/firmware.jed'
              match = jed_payload(reference) == jed_payload(generated)
              results[name] = {'jedec_programming_records_match': match,
                               'legacy_jed_sha256': digest(reference), 'generated_jed_sha256': digest(generated)}
              results[name].update(compare_reports(reference, generated.parent / 'reports/firmware_impl'))
              print(name, results[name], flush=True)
              if not all(results[name][k] for k in ('pad_matches', 'mrp_matches')):
                  raise RuntimeError(f'{name}: pin/utilization reports differ')
              if not match:
                  raise RuntimeError(f'{name}: legacy/generated JEDEC payload mismatch; see {dest}')
          # Fresh checkout-shaped tree, with spaces in its path and no generated outputs.
          relocated = stage / 'relocated checkout'; relocated.mkdir()
          for folder in ('buildsystem', 'targets', 'programs'):
              shutil.copytree(ROOT / folder, relocated / folder, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('__pycache__'))
          scaffold(relocated, 'custom', 'tx30')
          artifacts = build_program(load_build(relocated, 'custom'))
          matches = jed_payload(artifacts / 'firmware.jed') == jed_payload(load_build(ROOT, 'tx30').directory / 'artifacts/firmware.jed')
          results['scaffold_in_relocated_checkout'] = {'jedec_programming_records_match': matches}
          if not matches:
              raise RuntimeError('Relocated scaffold differs from tx30')
          (stage / 'validation.json').write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2) + '\n')
          print(stage / 'validation.json')
      
      
      if __name__ == '__main__':
          main()

      Workspace layout
      ==================
      
      ``new_approach/`` can be copied or renamed and used independently. Within the
      current repository it is arranged as follows::
      
         uz_cpld/
         ├── MACHXO2/                 existing HDL, LPFs and released firmware
         ├── ispMACH/                 older device projects
         ├── Makefile                forwards commands into new_approach
         ├── .devcontainer/          VS Code discovery configuration
         ├── .github/workflows/      CI discovery configuration
         └── new_approach/
             ├── Makefile            build, simulation, tests and docs commands
             ├── .devcontainer/      unified Dockerfile, VS Code config and launchers
             ├── .gitignore          standalone generated-file exclusions
             ├── requirements.txt    build frontend Python dependencies
             ├── toolchain/          shared tooling package
             │   ├── buildsystem/    model, CLI, lifecycle and vendor backend
             │   ├── simulation/     shared pytest runner and dependencies
             │   ├── targets/        board metadata and strategy input
             │   ├── tests/          frontend and licensed integration checks
             │   └── build/          ignored aggregate test/validation results
             ├── programs/           self-contained program directories
             ├── docs/               this shared Sphinx project
             │   └── history/        earlier discussion and session records
             └── build/              preserved historical results
      
      Each program uses one directory with matching filenames::
      
         programs/tx30/
         ├── tx30.toml
         ├── tx30.vhdl
         ├── tx30_constraints.lpf
         ├── tx30_tb.py
         └── build/                 generated on demand; git ignored
             ├── uz_dslot_xo2/diamond/
             └── simulation/
      
      The TOML manifest names the local HDL, LPF and cocotb testbench. Compiler and
      simulator use these same local inputs. The initial HDL/LPF files were copied
      byte-for-byte from the old projects; they are independent files with no automatic
      synchronization. There is no central constraints directory.
      
      ``make new NAME=my_adapter TEMPLATE=tx30`` creates the same four-file layout,
      including an editable testbench copied from the current ``tx30`` program.
      ``TEMPLATE`` selects an existing program; no separate template files are stored. The workspace can be
      copied or renamed without sibling directories. An optional legacy comparison
      requires an explicit ``--legacy-project /path/to/project.ldf`` argument.
      
      Generated results
      ------------------
      
      * ``programs/<program>/build/<target>/diamond/`` contains project files, logs, firmware,
        reports and provenance.
      * ``programs/<program>/build/simulation/`` contains traces, test logs and run metadata;
        ``toolchain/build/simulation/junit.xml`` contains the pytest summary.
      * ``toolchain/build/validation/`` retains licensed scaffold checks and optional
        legacy-comparison evidence.
      * ``docs/_build/html/`` contains the generated documentation site.
      
      Local outputs produced before consolidation are preserved under
      ``build/history/pre-consolidation/`` when present. Their embedded paths describe
      the old layout; regenerate projects and outputs with the current commands.
      This archive is local evidence, not a source dependency.
      
      The workspace ``.gitignore`` excludes directories named ``build/`` at any depth.
      Cloning a program skips its generated build directory. ``make clean PROGRAM=...``
      removes only that program's selected target/backend output, preserving simulation
      results and the lock files under ``programs/<name>/build/.locks/``.
      
      Existing outputs in the old top-level ``build/`` are historical evidence. They
      are not moved into active program builds: generated Diamond projects contain
      relative source paths tied to their original locations. Generate fresh projects
      with ``make build`` or ``make project`` when using the new layout.
      Architecture and Python integration
      ====================================
      
      Make supplies convenient commands; :mod:`toolchain.buildsystem.cli` parses their arguments.
      :func:`toolchain.buildsystem.model.load_build` creates a validated :class:`toolchain.buildsystem.model.Build`.
      :mod:`toolchain.buildsystem.workflow` manages locks, regeneration, cleanup and provenance.
      :class:`toolchain.buildsystem.backends.diamond.DiamondBackend` handles vendor project
      preparation and build Tcl.
      
      From ``new_approach/``, use the Python API without shelling out to Make::
      
         from pathlib import Path
         from toolchain.buildsystem.model import load_build
         from toolchain.buildsystem.workflow import build_program
      
         config = load_build(Path("/path/to/new_approach"), "tx30")
         artifacts = build_program(config)
      
      The ``root`` argument is the standalone workspace directory containing
      ``programs/`` and ``toolchain/targets/``. Input paths cannot escape it. Build and simulation both
      read the same manifests and local VHDL copies under ``new_approach/programs/``.
      Each program directory also contains its LPF and cocotb testbench. Firmware outputs live under
      ``new_approach/programs/<program>/build/<target>/diamond/``; simulation results live under
      ``new_approach/programs/<program>/build/simulation/``.
      
      Importing these build modules does not invoke Diamond. Use workflow functions to retain
      locking and provenance guarantees; direct backend methods are lower-level helpers.
      Expected user/configuration failures raise :class:`toolchain.buildsystem.model.BuildError`.
      The CLI reports them with a nonzero exit status.
      
      Build lifecycle
      ---------------
      
      A build holds a lock outside its disposable directory, checks generated settings
      for external changes, removes previous artifacts, and generates a fresh project.
      Diamond Tcl imports a copied strategy and references the authored files. Because
      Diamond treats ``def_top`` as an internal Tcl option, the generator writes that
      option into the generated LDF XML after Tcl saves the project.
      
      The backend runs synthesis, translation, map, PAR, PAR timing, Bitgen and Jedecgen.
      Headless Tcl subprocesses receive no display variables and no interactive stdin.
      The separate GUI launcher inherits the host display environment.
      Success requires both nonempty exports from the fresh implementation directory,
      the required reported tool version, and unchanged input hashes across the build.
      Failure logs and intermediates remain available for diagnosis.
      
      ``build.json`` records hashes of HDL, LPF, strategy, program-local testbench, manifests and
      frontend Python files; Git revision/status; selected device, options and tool version; the launcher
      path/hash; report and firmware hashes; completion time and the build-log path.
      It is an audit record, not a reproducible-build proof. The mounted Diamond
      installation and unpinned OS packages remain external state. Preserve the logs
      alongside artifacts when publishing a release. Firmware publication and hardware
      qualification remain a separate process.
      
      Extending the system
      --------------------
      
      Additional backends should implement project preparation, build execution and
      artifact collection while keeping board and program definitions separate.
      Currently backend selection rejects everything except Diamond; no placeholder
      FOSS implementation claims successful builds. Device-specific primitives require
      review before reusing programs on other families.
      
      Future work includes reviewed catalog expansion, shared logic/constraints,
      container digest/package pinning, hardware programming, FOSS and ispMACH backends,
      and separate PDF/SVG netlist analysis. Earlier design discussions and
      implementation records are available in :doc:`history`.

## User

the test bench, e.g., tx26_w_enable_tb still seems overly complicated regarding syntax. What does for enable in range(16): do in the context of cocotb

## Assistant

`for enable in range(16):` is ordinary Python. It runs the indented code **16 times**, with `enable` taking values from `0` through `15`.

The four enable pins have **16 possible combinations** (`2⁴`). These lines assign each bit of that number to a pin:

```python
dut.fpga_26.value = enable & 1
dut.fpga_27.value = (enable >> 1) & 1
dut.fpga_28.value = (enable >> 2) & 1
dut.fpga_29.value = (enable >> 3) & 1
```

`>>` shifts a bit into position; `& 1` extracts it. For example:

| `enable` | FPGA pins 26, 27, 28, 29 | Forwarding allowed |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | 0, 0, 0, 0 | No |
| 12 | 0, 0, 1, 1 | Yes, unless safe state is requested |
| 15 | 1, 1, 1, 1 | No |

In cocotb, assigning `.value` drives the simulated input. The later `await Timer(...)` lets the HDL respond before checking outputs.

The loop tests that **only the correct enable combination allows forwarding**, and that all 15 incorrect combinations block it. The bit manipulation makes the code compact, but an explicit list of pin combinations would be easier to read.

## User

does tx26_w_enable_tb drive the simulation?

## Assistant

Yes. `tx26_w_enable_tb.py` drives the simulation by:

1. Setting the simulated FPGA data pins, enable pins, and safe-state request.
2. Letting the simulator advance with `await Timer(1, unit="ns")`.
3. Checking that the VHDL produces the expected outputs.

**GHDL executes the actual VHDL design; the cocotb testbench supplies inputs and checks its responses.**

Running:

```sh
make sim PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable
```

compiles the program’s VHDL and runs this testbench. The waveform records the resulting inputs and outputs.

## User

how is it determined for how long the simulation runs?

## Assistant

In this testbench, simulation runs **until the test function finishes**. There is no separately configured duration.

Each execution of:

```python
await Timer(1, unit="ns")
```

advances simulated time by **1 nanosecond**. The loops determine how many times this happens:

- **54 data patterns:** all zeros, all ones, 26 walking-one patterns, and 26 walking-zero patterns.
- **16 enable combinations** per pattern.
- **3 safe-state values** per combination: `0 → 1 → 0`.

Total simulated duration:

**54 × 16 × 3 × 1 ns = 2,592 ns = 2.592 µs**

An assertion failure ends the test early. The wall-clock time to compile and run it is separate from this simulated duration.

      Building and device programming are separate operations; the latter has a
      five-device D-slot chain and carrier-specific connection settings. See
      [programming documentation](https://ultrazohm.org/guide/CPLD/cpld_programming.html).

      Validation and acceptance
      ===========================
      
      From ``new_approach/``, run ``make test`` for frontend regressions, ``make sim``
      for HDL behavioral tests and waveforms, and ``make docs`` for a strict Sphinx
      build. The repository-root Makefile forwards all three commands. Actual tool validation uses ``make build-all`` with the mounted

      Tooling tests and hardware testbenches
      ---------------------------------------
      
      ``toolchain/tests/`` tests the Python build tooling itself. ``make test`` runs
      its regression suite without Diamond. Vendor preparation and compilation are
      mocked in those tests; they verify frontend behavior, not actual synthesis.
      The separate
      ``toolchain/tests/validate_diamond.py`` checks cloning and firmware generation
      with licensed Diamond; legacy comparison is optional.
      
      Hardware behavior is tested by ``programs/<name>/<name>_tb.py`` through
      ``make sim``. Those testbenches are kept with their programs.
      
      Routing semantics to preserve
      -------------------------------
      
      * ``tx30`` gates all 30 adapter outputs with ``not reqsafestate``.
      * ``rx30`` forwards adapter inputs directly to FPGA outputs; its ``slotok``
        reflects the safe-state request, but its data routing is not gated.
      * ``tx26_w_enable`` additionally requires the 0, 0, 1, 1 enable pattern on FPGA
        channels 26–29. Adapter outputs 26–29 are declared but undriven in the legacy HDL.
      
      All three drive ``reqoe`` high in their present source. Template generation and
      migration retain these definitions without refactoring safety logic.
      
      Manual release checks
      -----------------------
      
      1. Review pin/electrical reports against the board and adapter mapping.
      2. Review combinational delays and vendor warnings. These routing LPFs do not
         define a timing acceptance budget, so successful builds do not mean timing
         closure. Clocked programs need explicit clocks and timing requirements.
      3. Compare unchanged legacy and generated-project builds using the same tool,
         HDL, constraints and strategy. Ignore container paths and timestamp headers
         when comparing payloads and reports.

      uploads the HTML site.

      workflow does not supply a vendor license.

      Manifests and targets
      =====================
      
      Program manifest
      ----------------
      
      ``programs/<name>/<name>.toml`` explicitly lists inputs. Paths are relative to
      the manifest, must stay within the checkout, and must exist. No recursive source
      globbing is used. The catalog programs each declare ``SignalRouter`` and must
      be compiled separately. Their HDL is local to ``programs/<name>/`` and their
      LPFs are alongside them as ``<name>_constraints.lpf``. Each LPF is preserved separately, including
      its electrical settings and existing warnings; no shared constraint merging is
      performed.
      
      .. literalinclude:: ../programs/tx30/tx30.toml
         :language: toml
      
      ``name`` matches the directory and uses lowercase letters, digits and underscores,
      starting with a letter. ``top`` is the VHDL entity. ``standard`` is ``"1993"`` or
      ``"2008"``. ``sources`` is ordered and assigns each file to a VHDL library.
      ``testbench`` names the program-local ``<name>_tb.py`` cocotb file; the runner
      loads it explicitly rather than discovering unrelated tests.
      ``targets`` explicitly lists supported target names. The selected target must
      appear in that list. Exactly one authored LPF is supported in the first version.
      Constraint composition is deliberately rejected until conflict handling is
      implemented. Unknown fields, duplicate source paths and unsupported backends
      are errors. All fields shown in the program and target examples are required,
      including ``testbench`` and the empty ``diamond.options`` table. Build checks
      validate that the testbench file exists, but do not execute it. The source list
      must be nonempty; VHDL entity and library names must be valid basic identifiers.
      
      Target manifest
      ---------------
      
      .. literalinclude:: ../toolchain/targets/uz_dslot_xo2/target.toml
         :language: toml
      
      ``uz_dslot_xo2`` identifies the UltraZohm D-slot MachXO2 target. Its current
      hardware scope is the Rev05+ D-slot ``LCMXO2-2000HC-4TG100C``. The target name
      is separate from the backend and program. D-slot
      position belongs to the program's mapping or a future programming command;
      it is not a different toolchain. Only the specified XO2-2000 device is currently
      accepted. S2C, S3C and ispMACH are not implemented targets.
      
      ``diamond.strategy`` identifies the captured legacy strategy file, which is now
      an explicit input. ``diamond.version`` is the required version found in the Diamond build
      log. The current version extractor recognizes only ``3.14.0.<number>.<number>``;
      changing the manifest alone does not add support for a different release family. ``diamond.options`` maps Diamond Tcl strategy option names to string
      values. Example::
      
         [diamond.options]
         lse_opt_goal = "Balanced"
         par_place_effort_level = "5"
      
      VHDL standard is controlled by the program manifest; do not also set
      ``lse_vhdl2008`` here. Unknown vendor option names fail during preparation.
      The initial baseline preserves legacy options, including its preference-error
      handling. Review constraints and vendor warnings; do not interpret a successful
      process exit as proof of correct electrical assignments or timing closure.
      
      The initial catalog contains only ``tx30``, ``rx30`` and ``tx26_w_enable``.
      Existing program manifests also define the source for ``make new TEMPLATE=<name>``;
      there is no separate template metadata. Shared HDL extraction is a separate functional change.
      
      
      Future capability matching
      ---------------------------
      
      Capability matching is deferred. Neither ``capabilities`` nor ``requires`` is a
      current manifest field; the loader rejects these fields rather than ignoring
      them. Compatibility currently uses the program's explicit ``targets`` list.
      
      When multiple targets are supported, a target could advertise features such as
      ``machxo2``, ``s3c_safety_interface`` or ``internal_oscillator``, while a program
      could declare the features it requires. The loader would reject a selection
      unless all required features are available. This could catch incompatible
      program/board combinations before invoking a compiler.
      
      These labels would describe reviewed hardware and backend support. They would
      not generate HDL, enable physical features, inspect VHDL automatically, or make
      a program portable merely by changing a target flag. Reintroducing them would
      require defined meanings, reviewed target declarations, and validation tests.
      
      Target rename
      ---------------
      
      ``uz_dslot_xo2`` replaces the earlier name ``rev05_dslot``. CLI and Make defaults
      use the new name. Existing generated outputs under ``build/<program>/rev05_dslot/``
      remain historical local artifacts; new builds use
      ``programs/<program>/build/uz_dslot_xo2/``. Earlier session records retain the original name.

      import hashlib
      from importlib.metadata import version
      import json

      from cocotb_tools.runner import get_runner
      
      from toolchain.buildsystem.model import load_build

      ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
      
      
      def test_routing(program, request):
          """Compile manifest HDL, execute routing contracts and retain waveforms.
      
          ``program`` is selected by the pytest fixture in ``toolchain.simulation.conftest``;
          ``request`` supplies the seed and waveform format from command-line options.
          Results are written beneath ``new_approach/programs/<program>/build/simulation``.
          """
          build = load_build(ROOT, program)
          output = safe_directory(build, build.build_root / "simulation")
          output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
          # Never leave a previous successful run's waveform/results beside a failed
          # compilation. Preserve the directory itself (it contains GHDL's library).
          for pattern in ("waves.*", "*.result.xml", "*.log", "run.json"):
              for artifact in output.glob(pattern):
                  artifact.unlink()
          seed = request.config.getoption("--seed")
          wave_format = request.config.getoption("--wave-format")
          standard = {"1993": "93", "2008": "08"}[build.standard]
          # These three programs have only work-library sources. Fail explicitly if
          # their manifests grow dependencies that need a separate compilation step.
          assert all(s.library.lower() == "work" for s in build.sources)
          provenance = {
              "program": program, "seed": seed, "standard": build.standard,
              "python": sys.version,
              "cocotb": version("cocotb"), "pytest": version("pytest"),
              "wave_format": wave_format,
              "testbench": {str(build.testbench.relative_to(ROOT)):
                            hashlib.sha256(build.testbench.read_bytes()).hexdigest()},
              "ghdl": subprocess.check_output(["ghdl", "--version"], text=True),
              "sources": {str(s.path.relative_to(ROOT)):
                          hashlib.sha256(s.path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                          for s in build.sources},
          }
          (output / "run.json").write_text(json.dumps(provenance, indent=2) + "\n")
          runner = get_runner("ghdl")
          runner.build(
              sources=[s.path for s in build.sources], hdl_library="work",
              hdl_toplevel=build.top.lower(), build_args=[f"--std={standard}"],
              build_dir=output, always=True, log_file=output / "compile.log",
          )
          wave = output / f"waves.{wave_format}"
          runner.test(

              test_args=[f"--std={standard}"],
              plusargs=[f"--{'wave' if wave_format == 'ghw' else 'fst'}={wave}",
                        "--assert-level=error"],
              seed=seed,
              log_file=output / "simulation.log",
          )

## Assistant

The current `.ghw` files are GHDL’s native waveform format. I’ll make VCD the default portable export and use it to generate interactive Plotly plots. UltraZohm also uses Plotly in its Sphinx dependencies.

For netlists, I’ll use GHDL → Yosys → Graphviz and label the diagrams as RTL analysis, since they won’t represent Diamond’s placed-and-routed design. The remaining-work list is saved in `new_approach/toolchain_todo.md`.

## Assistant

Testing exposed a timing detail: GHDL’s VCD can omit the final interval when no signal changes, so the trace ended at 2591 ns even though the test ran for 2592 ns. I’ve updated the viewer to use cocotb’s recorded end time and extend the final values through that last interval.

      new_approach/docs/environments.rst:147:not install ``docs/requirements.txt``: its Sphinx version comes from apt, while
      new_approach/docs/environments.rst:148:that requirements file pins Sphinx 7.4.7 for a separate native Python setup.
      """Generate program pages from fresh RTL schematics and passing simulations."""
      import json
      from pathlib import Path
      import shutil
      import subprocess
      import sys
      
      from toolchain.analysis.netlist import ROOT, export_netlist
      from toolchain.analysis.waveform import write_waveform
      from toolchain.buildsystem.model import BuildError, load_build
      from toolchain.buildsystem.workflow import digest, write_json
      
      
      def generate(root=ROOT):
          """Build documentation assets for every program manifest, including clones."""
          generated = root / 'docs/_generated'
          if generated.is_symlink():
              raise BuildError('Generated documentation directory must not be a symlink')
          if generated.exists():
              shutil.rmtree(generated)
          pages = generated / 'programs'
          pages.mkdir(parents=True)
          names = sorted(p.parent.name for p in (root / 'programs').glob('*/*.toml')
                         if p.stem == p.parent.name)
          if not names:
              raise BuildError('No program manifests found')
          for name in names:
              build = load_build(root, name)
              netlist = export_netlist(build)
              before = {str(p.relative_to(root)): digest(p) for p in (*[s.path for s in build.sources], build.testbench)}
              subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', 'toolchain/simulation/test_simulation.py',
                              '--program', name, '--wave-format', 'vcd', '--seed', '1', '-q'], cwd=root, check=True)
              if before != {str(p.relative_to(root)): digest(p) for p in (*[s.path for s in build.sources], build.testbench)}:
                  raise BuildError(f'{name}: sources changed while generating documentation')
              net_inputs = json.loads((netlist / 'netlist.json').read_text())['inputs']
              if any(before[path] != value for path, value in net_inputs.items()):
                  raise BuildError(f'{name}: netlist and simulation use different HDL')
              simulation = build.build_root / 'simulation'
              run = json.loads((simulation / 'run.json').read_text())
              info = write_waveform(simulation / 'waves.vcd', simulation / 'waveform.html',
                                    f'{name} — RTL waveform', run['simulation_duration_ns'])
              write_json(simulation / 'waveform.json', {**info, 'inputs': before,
                         'vcd_sha256': digest(simulation / 'waves.vcd'), 'seed': 1})
              assets = generated / 'static/program-assets' / name
              assets.mkdir(parents=True)
              for src in [netlist / 'netlist.svg', netlist / 'netlist.pdf', netlist / 'netlist.json',
                          simulation / 'waveform.html', simulation / 'waves.vcd',
                          simulation / 'waveform.json', simulation / 'run.json']:
                  shutil.copy2(src, assets / src.name)
              intro = root / 'programs' / name / 'description.rst'
              description = (f'.. include:: ../../../programs/{name}/description.rst\n\n' if intro.is_file()
                             else 'This page is generated from the program manifest, HDL and cocotb testbench.\n\n')
              page = f'''{name}
      {'=' * len(name)}
      
      {description}Target: ``{build.target}``; top entity: ``{build.top}``.
      
      RTL netlist
      -----------
      
      FROM ubuntu:22.04
      
      ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
      RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
          bash ca-certificates curl git make python3 python3-pip libpython3.10 gtkwave python3-tomli python3-sphinx python3-tk ripgrep sudo yosys graphviz \
          iproute2 net-tools file procps \
          libfontconfig1 libfreetype6 libglib2.0-0 libice6 libsm6 \
          libx11-6 libxext6 libxft2 libxi6 libxrandr2 libxrender1 libxt6 libxtst6 \
          libncurses5 libtinfo5 libusb-0.1-4 libusb-1.0-0 libuuid1 zlib1g \
          && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
      
      RUN curl -fsSL https://github.com/ghdl/ghdl/releases/download/v4.1.0/ghdl-gha-ubuntu-22.04-mcode.tgz -o /tmp/ghdl.tgz \
          && echo '1ffa567ad50f54529140108ab45b974829ca134d47d095b0ed704d35cd2ff1d6  /tmp/ghdl.tgz' | sha256sum -c - \
          && mkdir -p /opt/ghdl && tar -xzf /tmp/ghdl.tgz -C /opt/ghdl \
          && rm /tmp/ghdl.tgz
      ENV PATH="/opt/ghdl/bin:${PATH}"
      ENV CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER=1
      ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
      COPY toolchain/simulation/requirements.txt /tmp/requirements.txt
      COPY toolchain/analysis/requirements.txt /tmp/analysis-requirements.txt
      RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir -r /tmp/requirements.txt -r /tmp/analysis-requirements.txt && ghdl --version
      
      ARG USERNAME=vscode
      ARG USER_UID=1000
      .DEFAULT_GOAL := build
      PYTHON ?= python3
      TARGET ?= uz_dslot_xo2
      TEMPLATE ?= tx30
      # Quote values as single shell arguments, including embedded apostrophes.
      quote = '$(subst ','"'"',$(1))'
      ARGS = --target $(call quote,$(TARGET)) $(if $(PROGRAM),--program $(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) $(if $(TOOLCHAIN),--toolchain $(call quote,$(TOOLCHAIN)))
      .PHONY: build list doctor new check project gui build-all clean test docs docs-local docs-assets-local netlist netlist-local sim sim-image sim-container test-container docs-container _sim
      build list doctor check project gui build-all:
      	$(PYTHON) -m toolchain.buildsystem $@ $(ARGS)
      new:
      	$(PYTHON) -m toolchain.buildsystem new $(ARGS) --name $(call quote,$(NAME)) --template $(call quote,$(TEMPLATE))
      clean:
      	$(PYTHON) -m toolchain.buildsystem clean $(ARGS) $(if $(filter 1,$(DISCARD_PROJECT_CHANGES)),--discard-project-changes)
      test:
      	$(PYTHON) -m unittest discover -s toolchain/tests -v
      CONTAINER_ENGINE ?= docker
      SIM_IMAGE ?= uz-cpld-toolchain
      # Bind source for commands run from the host.
      SIM_WORKSPACE ?= $(CURDIR)
      SEED ?= 1
      WAVE_FORMAT ?= vcd
      CONTAINER_RUN = $(CONTAINER_ENGINE) run --rm --user "$$(id -u):$$(id -g)" --mount $(call quote,type=bind$(comma)source=$(SIM_WORKSPACE)$(comma)target=/work) -w /work $(call quote,$(SIM_IMAGE))
      comma := ,
      sim-image:
      	@command -v $(CONTAINER_ENGINE) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Container engine missing. Install Docker on the host or reopen in the unified Dev Container." >&2; exit 1; }
      	$(CONTAINER_ENGINE) build -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile -t $(call quote,$(SIM_IMAGE)) .
      ifeq ($(CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER),1)
      sim: _sim
      test-container: test
      docs: docs-local
      netlist: netlist-local
      else
      sim: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make _sim $(if $(PROGRAM),PROGRAM=$(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) SEED=$(call quote,$(SEED)) WAVE_FORMAT=$(call quote,$(WAVE_FORMAT))
      test-container: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make test
      netlist: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make netlist-local $(if $(PROGRAM),PROGRAM=$(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) TARGET=$(call quote,$(TARGET))
      docs: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make docs-local
      endif
      # Compatibility alias.
      sim-container: sim
      docs-container: docs
      # Image-internal entry point. Never creates or selects a host virtual environment.
      _sim:
      	@test "$(CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER)" = "1" || { echo "Use 'make sim' to run in the simulation container." >&2; exit 1; }
      	python3 -m pytest toolchain/simulation/test_simulation.py -v --junitxml=toolchain/build/simulation/junit.xml $(if $(PROGRAM),--program $(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) --seed $(call quote,$(SEED)) --wave-format $(call quote,$(WAVE_FORMAT))
      netlist-local:
      	$(PYTHON) -m toolchain.analysis.netlist --target $(call quote,$(TARGET)) $(if $(PROGRAM),--program $(call quote,$(PROGRAM)))
      docs-assets-local:
      	$(PYTHON) -m toolchain.analysis.documentation
      docs-local: docs-assets-local
      	$(PYTHON) -m sphinx -W --keep-going -b html docs docs/_build/html

      # UltraZohm CPLD
      
      Legacy hardware projects and released firmware remain in `MACHXO2/` and `ispMACH/`.
      The build system, simulator, manifests, tooling self-tests, containers and shared
      Sphinx documentation are consolidated in [`new_approach/`](new_approach/README.md).
      
      From this directory, `make build PROGRAM=tx30`, `make sim`, `make test`, and
      `make docs` forward to the tooling workspace. Generated outputs are under
      `new_approach/programs/<name>/build/`, with aggregate validation results in
      `new_approach/toolchain/build/`; the documentation is generated in
      `new_approach/docs/_build/html/`.
      
      `make docs` uses the installed tools inside the Dev Container and the shared
      container image on the host. Use `make docs-local` to run the complete documentation pipeline
      with locally installed tools. `make docs-container` remains an alias for `make docs`.
      # Development container entry point
      
      VS Code discovers `devcontainer.json` here. The image and launcher scripts live
      in [`new_approach/.devcontainer`](../new_approach/.devcontainer).
      
      See the shared [environment guide](../new_approach/docs/environments.rst) for
      Diamond installation mounts, licensing, simulator setup, and documentation builds.
