      Specific comments for project optical_14tx_4rx_2L_interlock
      """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
      
      This project is intended for a two-level three-phase inverter, that consists of three half-bridges connected in the following way:
      
      fpga_00 -> d_00 -> phase A
      fpga_01 -> d_01 -> phase A
      
      fpga_02 -> d_02 -> phase B
      fpga_03 -> d_03 -> phase B
      
      fpga_04 -> d_04 -> phase C
      fpga_05 -> d_05 -> phase C
      
      The switches in each phase/half-bridge/switching-cell are interlocked, such that it is not possible that both are HIGH at the same time, preventing a short-circuit, using the following logic:
      
         d_00 = fpga_00 & enable_signal & !fpga_01 ;
         d_01 = fpga_01 & enable_signal & !fpga_00 ;
      
      There is no dead-time implemented on the CPLD. Check the top_level.abl to see the implemented logic, it starts after the keyword EQUATIONS.
      A detailed description can be found on docs.ultrazohm.com -> CPLD
      
      
      Specific comments for project optical_14tx_4rx_3L_interlock
      """""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
      
      This project is intended for a three-level three-phase inverter, that consists of three phases connected in the following way:
      
      fpga_00 -> d_00 -> phase A - Top
      fpga_01 -> d_01 -> phase A - Neutral Point Upper
      fpga_02 -> d_02 -> phase A - Neutral Point Lower
      fpga_03 -> d_03 -> phase A - Bottom
      
      fpga_04 -> d_04 -> phase B - Top
      fpga_05 -> d_05 -> phase B - Neutral Point Upper
      fpga_06 -> d_06 -> phase B - Neutral Point Lower
      fpga_07 -> d_07 -> phase B - Bottom
      
      fpga_08 -> d_08 -> phase C - Top
      fpga_09 -> d_09 -> phase C - Neutral Point Upper
      fpga_10 -> d_10 -> phase C - Neutral Point Lower
      fpga_11 -> d_11 -> phase C - Bottom
      
      The switches in each switching-cell are interlocked, such that it is not possible that both are HIGH at the same time, preventing a short-circuit as well as undesired switch positions, using the following logic:
      
         "interlock of switching cell 1 in phase A
         d_00 = fpga_00 & enable_signal & !fpga_02 ;
         d_02 = fpga_02 & enable_signal & !fpga_00 ;
      
         "interlock of switching cell 2 in phase A
         d_01 = fpga_01 & enable_signal & !fpga_03 ;
         d_03 = fpga_03 & enable_signal & !fpga_01 ;
      
      There is no dead-time implemented on the CPLD. This projects was made on software: Quartus 16
      The projects are for a PCB that was made by Usach team, but the idea is to use the communication modules.Build and author programs
      =========================
      
      Complete :doc:`environments` first. Commands below run from ``new_approach/``.
      The repository-root Makefile forwards the same commands here.
      
      Build the catalog::
      
         make list
         make doctor
         make check PROGRAM=tx30
         make build PROGRAM=tx30
         make build-all
      
      ``check`` validates inputs without Diamond. ``doctor`` also checks Tcl startup;
      it does not establish synthesis or export success. ``build-all`` processes the
      explicit catalog and returns failure if any catalog entry fails.
      
      Outputs are under ``programs/<program>/build/<target>/<backend>/``:
      
      * ``project/``: generated LDF, strategy, Tcl, and tool intermediates.
      * ``logs/``: timestamped preparation/build logs, retained across builds.
      * ``artifacts/``: fresh ``firmware.jed``, ``firmware.bit``, reports and ``build.json``.
      * ``configuration.json``: hashes used to detect edited generated settings.
      * ``status.json``: status of the last build that passed the initial guards.
      
      Once a build passes the lock and generated-configuration guards, it removes
      previous artifacts; failures during preparation or compilation leave no current
      artifacts and preserve available logs. An earlier rejection, such as invalid
      inputs, an active lock or edited generated settings, leaves previous outputs
      and status untouched. ``project`` regenerates project files without refreshing
      firmware or build status; consult ``build.json`` for the inputs of an export.
      Build operations never program a device. Existing released firmware in legacy directories is
      preserved.
      
      Create a program
      ----------------
      
      Clone an existing program and edit the resulting files::
      
         make new NAME=my_adapter TEMPLATE=tx30
         # Edit my_adapter.vhdl, my_adapter_constraints.lpf and my_adapter_tb.py
         # inside programs/my_adapter/.
         make check PROGRAM=my_adapter
         make sim PROGRAM=my_adapter
         make build PROGRAM=my_adapter
      
      ``TEMPLATE`` names an existing program directory, defaulting to ``tx30``.
      A program supporting the selected target can be the source, including one you
      created yourself. The command copies its current authored files, renames the four primary files, and
      updates manifest references while preserving source order, libraries, target
      support, HDL entity names and testbench behavior. Additional local files are
      copied too; Generated ``build/`` directories and Python caches are excluded. There is no separate ``templates/`` tree.
      The primary HDL must be named ``<template>.vhdl`` and listed in its manifest.
      Inputs outside the source program directory must be localized before cloning;
      symlinks within that directory are rejected.
      The clone is independent: future edits to the original do not update it.
      The generated manifest is ``programs/<name>/<name>.toml``. Creation refuses an
      existing destination. New programs are not automatically added to ``build-all``;
      review their behavior and constraints before adding them to
      ``programs/catalog.toml``.
      
      The ``tx26_w_enable`` program forwards channels 0–25 when FPGA channels 26–29 are
      0, 0, 1, 1 and ``reqsafestate`` is low. Its declared outputs 26–29 remain
      undriven, matching the legacy source. Review the reports when cloning this program.
      
      The build frontend commands are also available through Python, for example::
      
         python3 -m toolchain.buildsystem build --program tx30 --target uz_dslot_xo2
         python3 -m toolchain.buildsystem --help
      
      The Python CLI provides ``list``, ``doctor``, ``new``, ``check``, ``project``,
      ``build``, ``gui``, ``build-all`` and ``clean``. Simulation, tooling tests,
      documentation and container commands are separate Make targets. ``make`` without
      a target defaults to ``build`` and requires ``PROGRAM``. ``TARGET`` defaults to
      ``uz_dslot_xo2``; ``TOOLCHAIN`` selects the backend, currently only ``diamond``.
      
      GUI workflow
      ------------
      
      On a Linux host with a display and a native Diamond installation::
      
         make project PROGRAM=tx30
         make gui PROGRAM=tx30
      
      Generated projects reference authored HDL and LPF files using relative paths.
      Edits to those authored files persist. Verify the destination when saving from
      Spreadsheet View: an exported/generated LPF does not replace the authored LPF.
      Useful GUI changes to project membership or strategy must be transferred manually
      into manifests or the target strategy baseline.
      
      ``gui`` opens an existing project without regenerating it, preserving experiments.
      ``project`` and ``build`` regenerate settings and reject externally modified
      LDF/strategy/Tcl files. After transferring useful changes, discard generated work::
      
         make clean PROGRAM=tx30 DISCARD_PROJECT_CHANGES=1
      
      Ordinary ``make clean PROGRAM=tx30`` protects modified settings and removes only
      the selected generated directory. Authored inputs are preserved.
      
      Managed project/build/clean/GUI commands share a process lock. The GUI launcher
      must stay in the foreground until Diamond closes. A separately opened GUI cannot
      honor this lock; close it before starting a managed build. Container paths and
      host paths may differ: ``make project`` on the host can regenerate paths when
      needed. Native GUI interaction still requires the manual acceptance checks in
      :doc:`validation`.
      
      Manifests and targets
      =====================
      
      Program manifest
      ----------------
      
      ``programs/<name>/<name>.toml`` explicitly lists inputs. Paths are relative to
      the manifest, must stay within the checkout, and must exist. No recursive source
      globbing is used. The catalog programs each declare ``SignalRouter`` and must
      be compiled separately. Their HDL is local to ``programs/<name>/`` and their
      LPFs are alongside them as ``<name>_constraints.lpf``. Each LPF is preserved separately, including
      its electrical settings and existing warnings; no shared constraint merging is
      performed.
      
      .. literalinclude:: ../programs/tx30/tx30.toml
         :language: toml
      
      ``name`` matches the directory and uses lowercase letters, digits and underscores,
      starting with a letter. ``top`` is the VHDL entity. ``standard`` is ``"1993"`` or
      ``"2008"``. ``sources`` is ordered and assigns each file to a VHDL library.
      ``testbench`` names the program-local ``<name>_tb.py`` cocotb file; the runner
      loads it explicitly rather than discovering unrelated tests.
      ``targets`` explicitly lists supported target names. The selected target must
      appear in that list. Exactly one authored LPF is supported in the first version.
      Constraint composition is deliberately rejected until conflict handling is
      implemented. Unknown fields, duplicate source paths and unsupported backends
      are errors. All fields shown in the program and target examples are required,
      including ``testbench`` and the empty ``diamond.options`` table. Build checks
      validate that the testbench file exists, but do not execute it. The source list
      must be nonempty; VHDL entity and library names must be valid basic identifiers.
      
      Target manifest
      ---------------
      
      .. literalinclude:: ../toolchain/targets/uz_dslot_xo2/target.toml
         :language: toml
      
      ``uz_dslot_xo2`` identifies the UltraZohm D-slot MachXO2 target. Its current
      hardware scope is the Rev05+ D-slot ``LCMXO2-2000HC-4TG100C``. The target name
      is separate from the backend and program. D-slot
      position belongs to the program's mapping or a future programming command;
      it is not a different toolchain. Only the specified XO2-2000 device is currently
      accepted. S2C, S3C and ispMACH are not implemented targets.
      
      ``diamond.strategy`` identifies the captured legacy strategy file, which is now
      an explicit input. ``diamond.version`` is the required version found in the Diamond build
      log. The current version extractor recognizes only ``3.14.0.<number>.<number>``;
      changing the manifest alone does not add support for a different release family. ``diamond.options`` maps Diamond Tcl strategy option names to string
      values. Example::
      
         [diamond.options]
         lse_opt_goal = "Balanced"
         par_place_effort_level = "5"
      
      VHDL standard is controlled by the program manifest; do not also set
      ``lse_vhdl2008`` here. Unknown vendor option names fail during preparation.
      The initial baseline preserves legacy options, including its preference-error
      handling. Review constraints and vendor warnings; do not interpret a successful
      process exit as proof of correct electrical assignments or timing closure.
      
      The initial catalog contains only ``tx30``, ``rx30`` and ``tx26_w_enable``.
      Existing program manifests also define the source for ``make new TEMPLATE=<name>``;
      there is no separate template metadata. Shared HDL extraction is a separate functional change.
      
      
      Future capability matching
      ---------------------------
      
      Capability matching is deferred. Neither ``capabilities`` nor ``requires`` is a
      current manifest field; the loader rejects these fields rather than ignoring
      them. Compatibility currently uses the program's explicit ``targets`` list.
      
      When multiple targets are supported, a target could advertise features such as
      ``machxo2``, ``s3c_safety_interface`` or ``internal_oscillator``, while a program
      could declare the features it requires. The loader would reject a selection
      unless all required features are available. This could catch incompatible
      program/board combinations before invoking a compiler.
      
      These labels would describe reviewed hardware and backend support. They would
      not generate HDL, enable physical features, inspect VHDL automatically, or make
      a program portable merely by changing a target flag. Reintroducing them would
      require defined meanings, reviewed target declarations, and validation tests.
      
      Target rename
      ---------------
      
      ``uz_dslot_xo2`` replaces the earlier name ``rev05_dslot``. CLI and Make defaults
      use the new name. Existing generated outputs under ``build/<program>/rev05_dslot/``
      remain historical local artifacts; new builds use
      ``programs/<program>/build/uz_dslot_xo2/``. Earlier session records retain the original name.
      RTL simulation
      ==============
      
      The open-source simulation suite uses GHDL, cocotb, pytest, and GTKWave.
      It compiles the actual sources listed in the program manifests; Diamond and
      a license server are not required. Simulation currently covers ``tx30``,
      ``rx30``, and ``tx26_w_enable`` on the Rev05+ D-slot target ``uz_dslot_xo2``.
      
      Run the suite
      -------------
      
      Inside the Dev Container or with Docker available on the host (see :doc:`environments`), run from ``new_approach/``::
      
         make sim
         make sim PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable SEED=42
         make sim WAVE_FORMAT=fst
      
      On the host, ``make sim`` builds the cached image and runs the tests inside it;
      inside the Dev Container it runs directly with the installed tools. The root
      Makefile forwards the command. The host container workflow requires no host
      Python packages or GHDL. Both workflows consume the same manifests as
      :doc:`builds`; ``make test`` runs frontend regression tests, while ``make sim``
      executes the HDL tests. An unknown simulation program fails instead of silently
      running no tests.
      
      Inspect and reproduce failures
      ------------------------------
      
      Every simulation writes to ``programs/<program>/build/simulation/``:
      
      * ``waves.vcd``: portable text waveform containing the complete cocotb regression run.
      * ``compile.log`` and ``simulation.log``: compiler output and test assertions.
      * ``*.result.xml``: cocotb test results.
      * ``run.json``: random seed, simulator/Python versions, and source hashes.
      
      Paths here are relative to ``new_approach/``. The pytest summary is
      ``toolchain/build/simulation/junit.xml``. CI uploads both the aggregate summary
      and each program's simulation directory even after failures. Download and extract the artifact, then open the waveform::
      
         gtkwave programs/tx26_w_enable/build/simulation/waves.vcd
      
      Add the top-level data and safety signals from GTKWave's signal tree. VCD is the
      default. ``make sim WAVE_FORMAT=ghw`` additionally preserves VHDL types in GHW;
      ``make sim WAVE_FORMAT=fst`` additionally produces smaller FST traces.
      Use ``make docs`` to embed an interactive Plotly view in each program page;
      see :doc:`program-documentation`.
      The current tests are deterministic. ``SEED`` remains available in the runner
      and ``run.json`` for programs that later add randomized stimulus.
      Rerunning a program replaces its logs, results, and waveforms; copy
      artifacts elsewhere before comparing runs. Concurrent runs of the same program/target are rejected by the managed build
      lock; use separate checkouts for concurrent work.
      
      Behavior under test
      -------------------
      
      Each program has one short, dedicated test function in its own ``<name>_tb.py``.
      There is no program selector or generic routing helper inside these files.
      All-zero, all-one, walking-one and walking-zero patterns check every data route.
      For each pattern, the safe-state request goes from 0 to 1 and back to 0.
      The enable-controlled program checks all 16 enable codes for each pattern.
      Pilot, carrier-ready, SCL and SDA are held at zero. Randomized transitions and
      exhaustive auxiliary-input combinations are omitted to keep these tests simple.
      
      ``tx30`` and ``tx26_w_enable`` force transmitted data low during a safe-state
      request. ``rx30`` continues receiving data during safe state, while deasserting
      ``slotok``. All three programs hold ``reqoe`` high. These distinctions are
      explicit test contracts, not a claim that every program has identical safety
      behavior. The four unused D-slot outputs of ``tx26_w_enable`` are not driven by
      the RTL and are not treated as valid data outputs in these tests.
      
      Why async is used
      -------------------
      
      Cocotb test functions are coroutines, so they use ``async def``. After assigning
      inputs, ``await Timer(1, unit="ns")`` pauses the Python test and lets the HDL
      simulator advance. The test then reads the settled outputs. This is simulation
      time, not a wall-clock sleep or a measured propagation-delay requirement.
      
      These tests execute sequentially and start no concurrent tasks. Plain helper
      functions that do not wait on the simulator can use ordinary ``def``. A VHDL
      native testbench could use ``wait for`` instead, but Python cocotb uses
      ``async``/``await`` for that coordination. See the
      `cocotb testbench guide <https://docs.cocotb.org/en/v2.0.0/writing_testbenches.html>`_.
      
      Extending verification
      ----------------------
      
      Place the testbench in ``programs/<name>/<name>_tb.py`` and reference it with
      ``testbench`` in ``<name>.toml``. ``make sim PROGRAM=<name>`` runs that module;
      without ``PROGRAM``, simulation selects the explicit catalog. Source order,
      top entity, and VHDL standard come from the existing manifests. The runner always selects the default ``uz_dslot_xo2`` target; Make
      ``TARGET`` and ``TOOLCHAIN`` overrides are not passed to simulation. The initial
      runner accepts only ``work`` sources; additional libraries need explicit
      compilation before elaboration.
      
      The three initial programs need no vendor primitives; their unused
      ``library machxo2`` declarations were removed from the program sources.
      For future oscillator/EFB users, introduce wrappers and explicit behavioral
      models. Do not silently replace hardware primitives with empty stubs. Model
      tests should cover reset, bus errors, and timing assumptions. RTL simulation
      does not replace implementation timing analysis or hardware validation.
      
      For software cosimulation, retain UltraZohm's Ceedling unit tests and add a
      separate integration layer: host-compiled C driver, hardware-access adapter,
      cocotb transactions, and simulated HDL. Blocking C calls need a bridge that
      lets simulator time advance. Drivers accessing FPGA IP through AXI also need
      that IP or a documented model between the driver and CPLD. No C bridge or
      processor emulator is included in this initial suite.
      
      References
      ----------
      
      * `cocotb simulator support <https://docs.cocotb.org/en/v2.0.0/simulator_support.html>`_
      * `GHDL waveforms <https://ghdl.github.io/ghdl/using/Simulation.html>`_
      * `UltraZohm software unit tests <https://docs.ultrazohm.com/software/unit_tests/unit_tests.html>`_
      * `UltraZohm resolver interface <https://ultrazohm.org/ip_cores/uz_resolverIP/uz_resolverIP.html>`_
      Program documentation and netlists
      ==================================
      
      Build all program pages, diagrams and interactive waveforms with::
      
         make docs
      
      Open ``docs/_build/html/index.html`` and choose **Programs**. The command finds
      all ``programs/<name>/<name>.toml`` manifests, including programs outside the
      firmware catalog. For each program it exports a generic RTL netlist, runs the
      actual cocotb testbench with seed 1, renders the VCD as an interactive Plotly
      waveform, and builds its Sphinx page. Failed analysis or simulation stops the
      documentation build; old generated program pages are removed before generation.
      No Diamond installation or license is needed for this analysis.
      
      Authoring
      ---------
      
      Put explanatory reStructuredText in ``programs/<name>/description.rst``.
      This optional description is included at the top of the generated program page.
      ``make new`` copies it along with the HDL, constraints and testbench. Edit the
      copied description and test contract for the new program. Page headings,
      netlist images, downloads and waveform frames are generated automatically.
      
      ``make docs-local`` runs the same full pipeline with locally installed tools;
      ``make docs-assets-local`` generates the program pages and assets without running
      Sphinx. Direct ``python3 -m sphinx`` can render existing assets, but does not
      regenerate them after HDL or testbench edits. Use Make for a fresh result.
      
      Netlist export
      --------------
      
      Export diagrams without running simulation or building Sphinx::
      
         make netlist PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable
         make netlist
      
      With no ``PROGRAM``, this command exports the firmware catalog. On the host it
      uses the shared container image; in the Dev Container it runs directly.
      ``make netlist-local`` explicitly uses native tools.
      
      Files are placed in ``programs/<name>/build/netlist/``:
      
      * ``netlist.svg`` and ``netlist.pdf``: diagrams for embedding and download.
      * ``rtl.v``: GHDL's synthesized Verilog representation.
      * ``rtl.json`` and ``netlist.dot``: Yosys/Graphviz intermediate representations.
      * ``netlist.ys`` and tool logs: exact Yosys steps and diagnostic warnings.
      * ``netlist.json``: source hashes, producing tool versions and output hashes.
      
      GHDL elaborates the manifest sources using their VHDL standard; Yosys lowers
      processes, flattens hierarchy and cleans unused wiring; Graphviz renders the
      graph. This is **generic RTL analysis**, not Diamond's Netlist Analyzer output.
      It does not apply LPF constraints or perform device mapping, placement, routing
      or timing analysis. Attributes such as ``syn_keep`` may be ignored by GHDL.
      The current path supports ``work`` sources and programs without unsupported
      vendor primitives. Unsupported designs fail rather than using dummy primitives.
      
      Waveforms
      ---------
      
      ``make sim`` now defaults to **VCD (Value Change Dump)**, a text waveform format
      accepted by GTKWave and other waveform viewers. The previous default, GHW, is
      GHDL's native format. Select it explicitly when VHDL type information is useful::
      
         make sim PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable
         make sim PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable WAVE_FORMAT=ghw
         make sim PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable WAVE_FORMAT=fst
      
      VCD is always emitted; selecting GHW or FST produces that format alongside it.
      ``make docs`` reruns simulation in VCD mode, replacing prior simulation outputs.
      The Plotly viewer is generated by the documentation pipeline from the actual
      VCD transitions, not by repeating the expected behavior in Python.
      
      Choose a channel plus controls, or **All signals**. The initial view shows the
      first 150 ns; select **Full trace** to see the whole regression. Drag to zoom, double-click
      to reset, and hover for values. Signals use step lines and the time axis is in
      nanoseconds. All transitions are retained; a wide overview can look dense.
      Unknown/uninitialized values (X/U), high impedance (Z) and other nonbinary
      states use a middle level with the original value in the tooltip. Bus values
      are normalized to their width for display, with binary values on hover.
      VCD preserves timestamped values but not VHDL delta cycles; the last value at
      a timestamp is displayed. The viewer extends the last value to the simulation
      end time recorded by cocotb when the VCD omits the final stable interval.
      Digital test delays are not measured device delays.
      
      Each program's ``build/simulation/`` contains ``waves.vcd``, the normal test
      logs/results and ``run.json``. Documentation generation additionally creates
      ``waveform.html`` and ``waveform.json``. The HTML includes Plotly.js so it works
      offline. Downloads and embedded frames are copied into the Sphinx output;
      sharing the whole ``docs/_build/html/`` directory preserves the pages.
      
      Dependencies and references
      ----------------------------
      
      The shared Dockerfile installs GHDL, Yosys, Graphviz, Sphinx, simulation packages
      and ``toolchain/analysis/requirements.txt`` (Plotly and pyvcd). Rebuild the image
      after this change. Native users need those executable tools and the Python
      packages in ``docs/requirements.txt``. This feature does not implement a FOSS
      firmware backend or automated Diamond GUI export.
      
      UltraZohm's documentation also uses Sphinx and Plotly; this implementation uses
      standalone Plotly HTML embedded in Sphinx so the same waveform can be downloaded
      and opened independently.
      
      * `UltraZohm documentation dependencies <https://github.com/ultrazohm/ultrazohm_sw/blob/main/docs/requirements.txt>`_
      * `GHDL synthesis <https://ghdl.github.io/ghdl/using/Synthesis.html>`_
      * `Yosys schematic export <https://yosyshq.readthedocs.io/projects/yosys/en/0.47/cmd/show.html>`_
      * `Plotly HTML export <https://plotly.com/python/interactive-html-export/>`_
      * `pyvcd reader <https://pyvcd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/vcd.reader.html>`_
      
      Netlist exports and simulations use the same program/target lock as managed
      firmware operations. Run documentation, simulation and netlist commands
      sequentially for a given program; concurrent attempts fail rather than overwrite
      each other's active outputs.
      Environment setup
      ===================
      
      One Dockerfile, ``.devcontainer/Dockerfile``, provides the development and CI
      environment: Diamond runtime dependencies, GHDL, Python packages and Sphinx.
      Diamond itself still requires a mounted vendor installation and license.
      
      Simulation, tests and documentation
      -------------------------------------
      
      Install Docker Engine on the host. No host Python environment or GHDL install
      is needed for simulation. From the standalone workspace::
      
         make sim
         make test-container
         make docs
      
      Each command builds the same cached toolchain image and runs its task inside
      it. For CI or a full local check, ``make test-container docs-container sim``
      builds the image once for that Make invocation. Python dependencies and GHDL are
      installed in the image; no workspace virtual environment is created or selected.
      Open ``docs/_build/html/index.html`` after the documentation command.
      
      ``make docs`` generates fresh program diagrams and simulations, then runs Sphinx
      inside the Dev Container or shared host image. ``make docs-container`` is a compatibility alias for the same
      target. For an explicitly local build with installed analysis/simulation tools and Sphinx, use
      ``make docs-local``; ``PYTHON`` selects its Python executable. All documentation
      builds treat warnings as errors. Requesting ``docs`` and ``docs-container``
      together builds the site once. The repository-root Makefile forwards all requested
      targets in one sub-make so shared image prerequisites also run only once.
      
      ``make test`` and ``make docs-local`` are direct entry points for environments that
      already provide their tools, such as the Unified Dev Container. The frontend
      requires Python 3.10 or newer; Python 3.10 also needs ``tomli``. For a native
      Python setup, install ``requirements.txt`` for the frontend and
      ``docs/requirements.txt`` for documentation. The tooling tests also require the packages in
      ``toolchain/analysis/requirements.txt`` and ``tkinter`` (Ubuntu package ``python3-tk``) for Tcl quoting checks. CI uses the
      container commands above. Firmware commands such as ``make build`` always run
      in the calling environment, so run them inside the Dev Container or provide a
      native Diamond installation.
      
      Unified Dev Container
      -----------------------
      
      Install Docker Engine and VS Code's Dev Containers extension on native Linux.
      From the standalone ``new_approach/`` directory, before launching VS Code::
      
         export DIAMOND_HOST_ROOT="$HOME/lscc/diamond/3.14"
         code .
      
      Choose **Dev Containers: Reopen in Container**. The installation root is the
      parent of ``bin``, not ``bin/lin64``. If VS Code was already running without the
      variable, exit it fully and relaunch. The daemon must have access to that host
      path and the checkout.
      
      ``.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`` points to
      ``.devcontainer/Dockerfile`` with the standalone workspace as build context.
      The root repository configuration uses this same Dockerfile. The image provides
      all build, simulation and documentation dependencies, and the configuration mounts
      Diamond read-only at ``/opt/diamond``. No license files are copied into the image.
      After container recipe changes use **Rebuild Container**, or **Rebuild and Reopen
      in Container**; reopening alone may reuse the existing image. The repository bind
      mount persists, while unmounted container files and manually installed packages
      may be lost on rebuild. For temporary Ubuntu packages run ``sudo apt-get update``
      before ``sudo apt-get install``.
      
      Inside the Dev Container, ``make sim``, ``make test`` and ``make docs`` run
      directly using the installed tools. No Docker socket or nested container is
      needed. The ``test-container`` and ``docs-container`` aliases also run directly
      when the image's ``CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER=1`` marker is present.
      
      The image also includes curl, ripgrep and the standalone Codex CLI; VS Code requests
      its IDE extension. Authentication is performed inside the environment and is not
      baked into the image. ``CODEX_VERSION`` is a configurable build argument; cached
      layers do not automatically refresh its ``latest`` default.
      
      From the standalone workspace, direct container use is::
      
         docker build -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile -t uz-cpld-toolchain .
         docker run --rm --network=host \
           --mount "type=bind,source=$DIAMOND_HOST_ROOT,target=/opt/diamond,readonly" \
           --mount "type=bind,source=$PWD,target=/work" \
           uz-cpld-toolchain make build PROGRAM=tx30
      
      The default user is UID/GID 1000; VS Code adjusts it to the host user. Direct
      Docker users can set ``USER_UID`` and ``USER_GID`` at image build time. For rootless
      Podman, use the same recipe and ``--userns=keep-id`` on run commands. To use Podman
      with VS Code, configure ``dev.containers.dockerPath`` and add that Podman-specific
      run argument. The earlier CLI validation used Podman 3.4.2; VS Code attachment was
      not validated by that check.
      
      Launchers and licensing
      ------------------------
      
      .. list-table:: Runtime configuration
         :header-rows: 1
      
         * - Variable
           - Purpose
         * - ``DIAMOND_HOST_ROOT``
           - Host installation directory used by the Dev Container mount.
         * - ``DIAMOND_ROOT``
           - Runtime installation root; defaults to ``/opt/diamond``.
         * - ``DIAMOND_CLI`` / ``DIAMOND_GUI``
           - Python frontend launcher overrides: executable paths, not shell commands.
         * - ``LM_LICENSE_FILE``
           - Optional additional license file or ``port@server``.
      
      The vendor ``diamondc`` wrapper configures Tcl/shared libraries and prepends its
      installation's ``license/license.dat``. An extra license file needs a read-only
      mount and its container path. Native Linux host networking exposes host interfaces
      for the existing host-bound license; it is not a portable license guarantee or
      Docker Desktop networking configuration. Do not edit signed licenses or change
      host MAC addresses. Investigate vendor host-ID detection or authorized rehosting
      if licensing fails. Floating-license setups can use ``LM_LICENSE_FILE`` and need
      not inherently use host networking.
      
      Run ``check-diamond`` for Tcl startup and ``check-diamond --synthesis`` for the
      one-gate LSE smoke test. Dev Container creation automatically runs the startup
      check only. These shell helpers use ``DIAMOND_ROOT`` and do not read the Python
      frontend's ``DIAMOND_CLI`` override. The smoke test does not route or export firmware.
      ``make doctor`` validates the catalog and startup; ``make build-all`` exercises
      full exports. For GUI work set ``DIAMOND_ROOT`` to the native host installation
      and run ``make gui PROGRAM=tx30`` with a display; the container does not forward
      a desktop.
      
      Shared image and CI
      -------------------------
      
      From ``new_approach/``::
      
         make sim
         make sim PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable
         make sim WAVE_FORMAT=fst
      
      On the host, ``make sim`` first builds ``.devcontainer/Dockerfile`` using
      Docker's layer cache, then runs the selected program testbench in a disposable
      container. Inside the Dev Container it runs the testbench directly.
      The workspace is bind-mounted at ``/work``; logs and waveforms persist under
      ``programs/<name>/build/simulation/``. The container runs with the caller's UID/GID. Its internal
      ``_sim`` entry point invokes pytest directly, avoiding recursive container starts.
      ``sim-container`` is an alias for ``sim``; ``sim-image`` only builds the image.
      
      The image pins the Linux amd64 GHDL 4.1.0 archive by checksum and pins simulator
      Python dependencies in ``toolchain/simulation/requirements.txt``. Sphinx, Tcl test support
      and GTKWave are installed from Ubuntu packages in the image. The Dockerfile does
      not install ``docs/requirements.txt``: its Sphinx version comes from apt, while
      that requirements file pins Sphinx 7.4.7 for a separate native Python setup.
      The image also installs Yosys and Graphviz, plus the Plotly/pyvcd dependencies
      from ``toolchain/analysis/requirements.txt`` for program documentation. Dependency downloads occur during
      image builds, never in the workspace.
      
      ``CONTAINER_ENGINE`` defaults to ``docker`` and can select ``podman`` when running
      on a suitably configured host. ``SIM_IMAGE`` overrides the image tag, whose
      default is ``uz-cpld-toolchain``. The command requires a reachable container daemon;
      installing a CLI alone does not provide one. ``SIM_WORKSPACE`` overrides the host bind source when needed.
      
      The GitHub Actions workflow runs ``make -C new_approach test-container
      docs-container sim`` and uploads simulation evidence and the documentation site.
      It uses the same image and Make targets as local development.
      
      The mounted vendor installation, OS package updates and unpinned base image tags
      remain external inputs. See :doc:`validation` for what has actually been tested.

      Architecture and Python integration
      ====================================
      
      Make supplies convenient commands; :mod:`toolchain.buildsystem.cli` parses their arguments.
      :func:`toolchain.buildsystem.model.load_build` creates a validated :class:`toolchain.buildsystem.model.Build`.
      :mod:`toolchain.buildsystem.workflow` manages locks, regeneration, cleanup and provenance.
      :class:`toolchain.buildsystem.backends.diamond.DiamondBackend` handles vendor project
      preparation and build Tcl.
      
      From ``new_approach/``, use the Python API without shelling out to Make::
      
         from pathlib import Path
         from toolchain.buildsystem.model import load_build
         from toolchain.buildsystem.workflow import build_program
      
         config = load_build(Path("/path/to/new_approach"), "tx30")
         artifacts = build_program(config)
      
      The ``root`` argument is the standalone workspace directory containing
      ``programs/`` and ``toolchain/targets/``. Input paths cannot escape it. Build and simulation both
      read the same manifests and local VHDL copies under ``new_approach/programs/``.
      Each program directory also contains its LPF and cocotb testbench. Firmware outputs live under
      ``new_approach/programs/<program>/build/<target>/diamond/``; simulation results live under
      ``new_approach/programs/<program>/build/simulation/``.
      
      Importing these build modules does not invoke Diamond. Use workflow functions to retain
      locking and provenance guarantees; direct backend methods are lower-level helpers.
      Expected user/configuration failures raise :class:`toolchain.buildsystem.model.BuildError`.
      The CLI reports them with a nonzero exit status.
      
      Build lifecycle
      ---------------
      
      A build holds a lock outside its disposable directory, checks generated settings
      for external changes, removes previous artifacts, and generates a fresh project.
      Diamond Tcl imports a copied strategy and references the authored files. Because
      Diamond treats ``def_top`` as an internal Tcl option, the generator writes that
      option into the generated LDF XML after Tcl saves the project.
      
      The backend runs synthesis, translation, map, PAR, PAR timing, Bitgen and Jedecgen.
      Headless Tcl subprocesses receive no display variables and no interactive stdin.
      The separate GUI launcher inherits the host display environment.
      Success requires both nonempty exports from the fresh implementation directory,
      the required reported tool version, and unchanged input hashes across the build.
      Failure logs and intermediates remain available for diagnosis.
      
      ``build.json`` records hashes of HDL, LPF, strategy, program-local testbench, manifests and
      frontend Python files; Git revision/status; selected device, options and tool version; the launcher
      path/hash; report and firmware hashes; completion time and the build-log path.
      It is an audit record, not a reproducible-build proof. The mounted Diamond
      installation and unpinned OS packages remain external state. Preserve the logs
      alongside artifacts when publishing a release. Firmware publication and hardware
      qualification remain a separate process.
      
      Extending the system
      --------------------
      
      Additional backends should implement project preparation, build execution and
      artifact collection while keeping board and program definitions separate.
      Currently backend selection rejects everything except Diamond; no placeholder
      FOSS implementation claims successful builds. Device-specific primitives require
      review before reusing programs on other families.
      
      Future work includes reviewed catalog expansion, shared logic/constraints,
      container digest/package pinning, hardware programming, FOSS and ispMACH backends,
      and vendor-specific netlist export. Generic RTL SVG/PDF analysis and interactive
      program pages are implemented in ``toolchain/analysis/``; see
      :doc:`program-documentation`. Earlier design discussions and
      implementation records are available in :doc:`history`.
      Workspace layout
      ==================
      
      ``new_approach/`` can be copied or renamed and used independently. Within the
      current repository it is arranged as follows::
      
         uz_cpld/
         ├── MACHXO2/                 existing HDL, LPFs and released firmware
         ├── ispMACH/                 older device projects
         ├── Makefile                forwards commands into new_approach
         ├── .devcontainer/          VS Code discovery configuration
         ├── .github/workflows/      CI discovery configuration
         └── new_approach/
             ├── Makefile            build, simulation, tests and docs commands
             ├── .devcontainer/      unified Dockerfile, VS Code config and launchers
             ├── .gitignore          standalone generated-file exclusions
             ├── requirements.txt    build frontend Python dependencies
             ├── toolchain/          shared tooling package
             │   ├── buildsystem/    model, CLI, lifecycle and vendor backend
             │   ├── analysis/      RTL diagrams, VCD reader and program documentation
             │   ├── simulation/     shared pytest runner and dependencies
             │   ├── targets/        board metadata and strategy input
             │   ├── tests/          frontend and licensed integration checks
             │   └── build/          ignored aggregate test/validation results
             ├── programs/           self-contained program directories
             ├── docs/               this shared Sphinx project
             │   └── history/        earlier discussion and session records
             └── build/              preserved historical results
      
      Each program uses one directory with matching filenames::
      
         programs/tx30/
         ├── tx30.toml
         ├── tx30.vhdl
         ├── tx30_constraints.lpf
         ├── tx30_tb.py
         ├── description.rst        optional authored program documentation
         └── build/                 generated on demand; git ignored
             ├── uz_dslot_xo2/diamond/
             ├── netlist/
             └── simulation/
      
      The TOML manifest names the local HDL, LPF and cocotb testbench. Compiler and
      simulator use these same local inputs. The initial HDL/LPF files were copied
      byte-for-byte from the old projects; they are independent files with no automatic
      synchronization. There is no central constraints directory.
      
      ``make new NAME=my_adapter TEMPLATE=tx30`` copies the four required program files and optional description,
      including an editable testbench copied from the current ``tx30`` program.
      ``TEMPLATE`` selects an existing program; no separate template files are stored. The workspace can be
      copied or renamed without sibling directories. An optional legacy comparison
      requires an explicit ``--legacy-project /path/to/project.ldf`` argument.
      
      Generated results
      ------------------
      
      * ``programs/<program>/build/<target>/diamond/`` contains project files, logs, firmware,
        reports and provenance.
      * ``programs/<program>/build/simulation/`` contains traces, test logs and run metadata;
        ``toolchain/build/simulation/junit.xml`` contains the pytest summary.
      * ``toolchain/build/validation/`` retains licensed scaffold checks and optional
        legacy-comparison evidence.
      * ``programs/<program>/build/netlist/`` contains SVG/PDF diagrams and analysis logs.
      * ``docs/_generated/`` contains ignored program pages and assets regenerated by Make.
      * ``docs/_build/html/`` contains the generated documentation site.
      
      Local outputs produced before consolidation are preserved under
      ``build/history/pre-consolidation/`` when present. Their embedded paths describe
      the old layout; regenerate projects and outputs with the current commands.
      This archive is local evidence, not a source dependency.
      
      The workspace ``.gitignore`` excludes directories named ``build/`` at any depth.
      Cloning a program skips its generated build directory. ``make clean PROGRAM=...``
      removes only that program's selected target/backend output, preserving simulation
      results and the lock files under ``programs/<name>/build/.locks/``.
      
      Existing outputs in the old top-level ``build/`` are historical evidence. They
      are not moved into active program builds: generated Diamond projects contain
      relative source paths tied to their original locations. Generate fresh projects
      with ``make build`` or ``make project`` when using the new layout.

      Simulation runner
      -------------------
      
      Both workflows use :func:`toolchain.buildsystem.model.load_build`. The simulation runner
      is called by pytest with fixtures from ``toolchain/simulation/conftest.py``; it is not a
      second manifest parser. Its optional cocotb dependency is mocked during Sphinx
      imports, so API imports themselves need no simulator. The full ``make docs``
      pipeline runs simulation to populate the program pages.
      
      .. automodule:: toolchain.simulation.test_simulation
         :members:
      
      Cocotb contracts
      -----------------
      
      The runner loads ``programs.<name>.<name>_tb`` inside the simulator. Each
      program owns an editable contract, initially copied from the selected source program.
      
      Each file has one sequential test: ``test_tx30``, ``test_rx30``, or
      ``test_tx26_w_enable``. Signal names and channel counts are specific to that
      program. There is no program selector, conditional routing helper, or shared
      testbench code. The small amount of duplication keeps each file readable alone.

      """Generate program pages from fresh RTL schematics and passing simulations."""
      import json
      from pathlib import Path
      import shutil
      import subprocess
      import sys
      
      from toolchain.analysis.netlist import ROOT, export_netlist
      from toolchain.analysis.waveform import write_waveform
      from toolchain.buildsystem.model import BuildError, load_build
      from toolchain.buildsystem.workflow import digest, write_json
      
      
      def generate(root=ROOT):
          """Build documentation assets for every program manifest, including clones."""
          generated = root / 'docs/_generated'
          if generated.is_symlink():
              raise BuildError('Generated documentation directory must not be a symlink')
          if generated.exists():
              shutil.rmtree(generated)
          pages = generated / 'programs'
          pages.mkdir(parents=True)
          names = sorted(p.parent.name for p in (root / 'programs').glob('*/*.toml')
                         if p.stem == p.parent.name)
          if not names:
              raise BuildError('No program manifests found')
          for name in names:
              build = load_build(root, name)
              netlist = export_netlist(build)
              before = {str(p.relative_to(root)): digest(p) for p in (*[s.path for s in build.sources], build.testbench)}
              subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', 'toolchain/simulation/test_simulation.py',
                              '--program', name, '--wave-format', 'vcd', '--seed', '1', '-q'], cwd=root, check=True)
              if before != {str(p.relative_to(root)): digest(p) for p in (*[s.path for s in build.sources], build.testbench)}:
                  raise BuildError(f'{name}: sources changed while generating documentation')
              net_inputs = json.loads((netlist / 'netlist.json').read_text())['inputs']
              if any(before[path] != value for path, value in net_inputs.items()):
                  raise BuildError(f'{name}: netlist and simulation use different HDL')
              simulation = build.build_root / 'simulation'
              run = json.loads((simulation / 'run.json').read_text())
              info = write_waveform(simulation / 'waves.vcd', simulation / 'waveform.html',
                                    f'{name} — RTL waveform', run['simulation_duration_ns'])
              write_json(simulation / 'waveform.json', {**info, 'inputs': before,
                         'vcd_sha256': digest(simulation / 'waves.vcd'), 'seed': 1})
              assets = generated / 'static/program-assets' / name
              assets.mkdir(parents=True)
              for src in [netlist / 'netlist.svg', netlist / 'netlist.pdf', netlist / 'netlist.json',
                          simulation / 'waveform.html', simulation / 'waves.vcd',
                          simulation / 'waveform.json', simulation / 'run.json']:
                  shutil.copy2(src, assets / src.name)
              intro = root / 'programs' / name / 'description.rst'
              description = (f'.. include:: ../../../programs/{name}/description.rst\n\n' if intro.is_file()
                             else 'This page is generated from the program manifest, HDL and cocotb testbench.\n\n')
              page = f'''{name}
      {'=' * len(name)}
      
      {description}Target: ``{build.target}``; top entity: ``{build.top}``.
      
      RTL netlist
      -----------
      
      This is a generic RTL schematic produced by GHDL synthesis, Yosys process
      lowering/flattening and Graphviz. It does not apply LPF constraints or reproduce
      Diamond technology mapping, placement, routing or timing. Vendor-specific
      attributes may be ignored; warnings are retained in the program's netlist logs.
      
      .. image:: ../static/program-assets/{name}/netlist.svg
         :alt: Generic RTL netlist for {name}
         :width: 100%
         :target: ../../program-assets/{name}/netlist.svg
      
      Download :download:`SVG <../static/program-assets/{name}/netlist.svg>`,
      :download:`PDF <../static/program-assets/{name}/netlist.pdf>` or
      :download:`netlist provenance <../static/program-assets/{name}/netlist.json>`.
      
      Simulation waveform
      -------------------
      
      The program's actual cocotb testbench passed. This trace covers
      **{info['duration_ns']:g} ns** of simulated time and **{info['signal_count']} signals**.
      Choose a channel, zoom in by dragging, and hover to read exact values.
      Unknown and high-impedance values appear at mid-level, not as logic zero.
      The viewer includes Plotly locally and works without an internet connection.
      
      .. only:: html
      
         .. raw:: html
      
            <iframe src="../../program-assets/{name}/waveform.html" title="{name} simulation waveform" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:1px solid #ddd" loading="lazy"></iframe>
      
      Download the :download:`interactive waveform <../static/program-assets/{name}/waveform.html>`,
      :download:`VCD trace <../static/program-assets/{name}/waves.vcd>`,
      :download:`simulation provenance <../static/program-assets/{name}/run.json>` or
      :download:`waveform provenance <../static/program-assets/{name}/waveform.json>`.
      The VCD contains the regression stimulus, not an application example or a
      post-route timing simulation. VCD records timestamped values, not VHDL delta cycles.
      
      Testbench
      ---------
      
      .. literalinclude:: ../../../programs/{name}/{name}_tb.py
         :language: python
      '''
              (pages / f'program-{name}.rst').write_text(page)
          (pages / 'index.rst').write_text('Programs\n========\n\n'
              'Each page combines the authored description with freshly generated netlist and simulation evidence.\n\n'
              '.. toctree::\n   :maxdepth: 1\n\n' + ''.join(f'   program-{name}\n' for name in names))
          return pages
      
      
      def main():
          try:
              print(generate())
          except (BuildError, OSError, ValueError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as exc:
              print(f'Program documentation failed: {exc}', file=sys.stderr)
              return 1
          return 0
      
      
      if __name__ == '__main__':
          raise SystemExit(main())

entry fails.The default Make target is ``build`` and requires ``PROGRAM``.``TARGET`` defaults to ``uz_dslot_xo2`` and ``TOOLCHAIN`` selects the implemented backend, ``diamond``.Firmware commands run in the calling environment and never flash a device.Create a program----------------::   make new NAME=my_adapter TEMPLATE=tx30   make check PROGRAM=my_adapter   make sim PROGRAM=my_adapter   make build PROGRAM=my_adapterEdit the cloned VHDL, LPF, cocotb testbench and optional ``description.rst`` before validation.Cloning copies the selected program'"'s current files, preserves entity names and libraries, and excludes generated "'``build/`` directories and Python caches.It requires a listed ``<template>.vhdl`` primary source, program-local inputs and no authored symlinks, and refuses an existing destination.A clone is independent of its source and must be reviewed before adding it to the firmware catalog.Documentation includes all program manifests, including uncatalogued clones.Outputs and failures--------------------``programs/<name>/build/<target>/diamond/`` contains the generated ``project/``, retained ``logs/`` and published ``artifacts/``.Artifacts include ``firmware.jed``, ``firmware.bit``, reports and a ``build.json`` provenance record.``configuration.json`` detects changes to generated settings; ``status.json`` records builds that passed the initial guards.A build that passes the lock/configuration guards removes previous artifacts before invoking Diamond.Preparation or compilation failure preserves logs without publishing stale firmware.An earlier rejection, such as an invalid manifest or edited generated settings, leaves previous outputs untouched.``project`` regenerates project files without refreshing firmware; consult ``build.json`` for the inputs used by an export.GUI and cleanup---------------With a native Diamond installation and display::   make project PROGRAM=tx30   make gui PROGRAM=tx30   make clean PROGRAM=tx30Generated projects reference authored HDL and LPFs; edits to those files persist.Check the destination when saving from Spreadsheet View, because an exported LPF does not replace the authored input automatically.Transfer useful project/strategy changes into manifests or the target strategy before regenerating.``gui`` preserves an existing project, while ``project``, ``build`` and ordinary ``clean`` reject edited generated settings.After preserving useful changes, ``make clean PROGRAM=tx30 DISCARD_PROJECT_CHANGES=1`` explicitly discards them.Cleanup removes only the selected firmware directory and preserves simulation, netlist and lock files.Managed operations share a program/target lock; independently launched GUI sessions cannot honor it and must be closed before a build.'"''','configuration.rst': '''Manifest reference==================Program-------.. literalinclude:: ../programs/tx30/tx30.toml   :language: tomlAll shown fields are required."'``name`` matches its directory and uses lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.``top`` and source libraries are VHDL basic identifiers; ``standard`` is ``1993`` or ``2008``.``sources`` is a nonempty ordered list with no duplicate paths, and ``targets`` explicitly lists compatible board targets.Input paths are relative to the manifest, must exist and must stay within the workspace.Exactly one authored LPF is supported; constraint merging is excluded to avoid ambiguous precedence.``testbench`` must name the program-local ``<name>_tb.py`` file; manifest validation checks its existence but does not run it.``description.rst`` is optional program prose discovered by the documentation generator.Target------.. literalinclude:: ../toolchain/targets/uz_dslot_xo2/target.toml   :language: tomlThe supported target is the Rev05+ UltraZohm D-slot ``LCMXO2-2000HC-4TG100C``.A board target is separate from the backend, program mapping and eventual JTAG chain position.``diamond.strategy`` selects the captured strategy input; the empty ``diamond.options`` table is required and accepts string-valued vendor overrides.Set VHDL standard through the program manifest rather than ``lse_vhdl2008``.Unknown vendor options fail during Diamond preparation.``diamond.version`` must appear in the build log; the extractor recognizes the ``3.14.0.<number>.<number>`` release family.Unknown manifest fields and unsupported backends/devices are rejected.Feature declarations such as ``capabilities`` and ``requires`` are future extensions, not accepted fields.'"''','simulation.rst': '''Simulation and tests====================::   make test-container   make sim   make sim PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable SEED=42   make sim PROGRAM=tx30 WAVE_FORMAT=ghw   make sim PROGRAM=rx30 WAVE_FORMAT=fst"'``make test`` runs Python tooling regressions, including mocked vendor failures and VCD interpretation; it does not establish synthesis success.``make sim`` runs the catalog, or the single selected program, using the actual manifest HDL and its cocotb testbench.The runner selects ``uz_dslot_xo2`` and accepts ``work`` sources; Make target/backend overrides are not simulation parameters.A missing program or failed assertion produces a failing command.Behavior--------The tests apply all-zero, all-one, walking-one and walking-zero data patterns with safe-state transitions ``0 → 1 → 0``.``tx26_w_enable`` additionally tests all 16 combinations of its four enable pins.Pilot, carrier-ready and I2C inputs are held low; exhaustive auxiliary-input combinations and randomized stimulus are excluded.The tests are deterministic, while ``SEED`` is recorded for programs that use random stimulus.Cocotb drives inputs and checks outputs while GHDL executes the VHDL.``await Timer(1, unit="ns")`` advances simulated time by 1 ns; the test ends when its coroutine completes or an assertion fails.The complete tests span 186 ns for ``tx30`` and ``rx30``, and 2592 ns for ``tx26_w_enable``.These waits allow combinational logic to settle and are not device timing requirements.Results-------``programs/<name>/build/simulation/`` contains compiler/simulation logs, cocotb result XML, ``run.json`` provenance and ``waves.vcd``.VCD is a portable text waveform; optional GHW preserves GHDL/VHDL type information and optional FST is more compact.Selecting GHW or FST emits that file alongside VCD.``toolchain/build/simulation/junit.xml`` is the aggregate pytest report.Reruns replace program results, and concurrent managed operations on the same program/target are rejected.Open VCD with GTKWave or use the interactive :doc:`program pages <program-documentation>`::   gtkwave programs/tx26_w_enable/build/simulation/waves.vcd'"''','program-documentation.rst': '''Program diagrams and waveforms==============================::   make docs   make netlist PROGRAM=tx26_w_enable"'``make docs`` discovers every program manifest, generates RTL schematics, runs its testbench with seed 1 and builds a Sphinx page.Each page includes ``programs/<name>/description.rst`` when present, SVG/PDF diagrams, an interactive waveform and downloads.Failed analysis or simulation stops the build; generated page sources are replaced before generation.``make netlist`` exports diagrams for the firmware catalog without simulation; ``PROGRAM`` selects one program.RTL netlists------------GHDL synthesizes the manifest'"'s VHDL to Verilog, Yosys lowers processes and flattens/cleans the generic netlist, and Graphviz renders SVG and PDF.This analysis excludes LPF constraints, device mapping, placement, routing and timing, so it does not represent Diamond's implemented netlist.Vendor attributes such as "'``syn_keep`` can be ignored, and unsupported primitives or non-``work`` libraries require explicit support.``programs/<name>/build/netlist/`` contains ``netlist.svg``, ``netlist.pdf``, source/tool/output provenance, intermediates and diagnostic logs.Netlist exports use the managed program/target lock and remove stale diagrams on failure.Interactive waveforms---------------------Plotly renders the actual VCD transitions as step traces with nanosecond units, channel selection, zoom and value tooltips.The initial view covers 150 ns; **Full trace** shows the complete test.Unknown/uninitialized values (X/U), high impedance (Z) and other nonbinary states retain their labels and use a middle display level.Bus values are normalized to their width, with binary values in tooltips.VCD has no delta-cycle axis, so the viewer shows the final value at each timestamp and extends it to the end time reported by cocotb.Documentation generation writes ``waveform.html`` and ``waveform.json`` beside the simulation results and copies public assets into the site.Each viewer embeds Plotly.js for offline use, trading larger HTML files for independence from external scripts.``make docs`` replaces simulation outputs with its VCD run; copy results before comparing separate runs.Authoring and publishing------------------------Write program-specific prose in ``description.rst`` and shared guides in ``docs/*.rst``.Use one sentence per source line without manual wrapping or a line-length limit; preserve the required layout of directives, tables and code blocks.Generated pages follow the same prose rule.``make docs-local`` uses installed tools; ``make docs-assets-local`` generates pages/assets without Sphinx.Direct Sphinx invocation renders existing assets without refreshing simulation or netlists.See :doc:`publishing` for GitHub Pages deployment and :doc:`architecture` for source/output ownership.References----------* `GHDL synthesis <https://ghdl.github.io/ghdl/using/Synthesis.html>`_* `Yosys schematic export <https://yosyshq.readthedocs.io/projects/yosys/en/0.47/cmd/show.html>`_* `Plotly HTML export <https://plotly.com/python/interactive-html-export/>`_* `UltraZohm documentation dependencies <https://github.com/ultrazohm/ultrazohm_sw/blob/main/docs/requirements.txt>`_'"''','architecture.rst': '''Architecture and tradeoffs==========================Source layout-------------::   new_approach/   ├── Makefile   ├── .devcontainer/          image stages and optional Diamond configuration   ├── toolchain/   │   ├── buildsystem/        validated model, CLI, lifecycle and Diamond backend   │   ├── simulation/         pytest/GHDL runner   │   ├── analysis/           RTL export, VCD viewer and Sphinx page generation   │   ├── targets/            board manifests and strategy inputs   │   └── tests/              tooling regressions and licensed integration check   ├── programs/<name>/        TOML, VHDL, LPF, testbench and description.rst   └── docs/                  shared Sphinx sourceThe workspace can be copied or renamed without the legacy repository.Program inputs are independent copies; changes to legacy projects do not synchronize automatically.Generated files live under each program's ignored "'``build/`` directory, while aggregate reports use ``toolchain/build/`` and documentation uses ``docs/_generated/`` and ``docs/_build/``.The repository-root Makefile forwards requested targets in one sub-make so shared prerequisites run once.Design decisions----------------Explicit manifests avoid accidentally combining programs that share the same top-level entity name.Per-program LPFs preserve adapter electrical settings; sharing constraints requires reviewed conflict handling.Cloning editable files keeps authoring simple but deliberately duplicates code and requires independent maintenance.Generated Diamond metadata keeps builds scriptable while retaining GUI access; useful GUI settings require manual transfer to authored configuration.Board and backend separation permits extensions, but changing a target flag cannot make device-specific HDL portable.The workflow validates inputs, acquires a lock, protects edited generated settings and creates a fresh project.Diamond runs synthesis, translation, mapping, place-and-route, timing reporting and both firmware exports without a display or interactive stdin.Because Diamond'"'s Tcl interface treats "'``def_top`` as internal, preparation sets it in the saved LDF XML.Publication requires nonempty exports, the configured tool version and unchanged input hashes.``build.json`` records inputs, options, tool/launcher identity, Git state, reports and output hashes; it is an audit record rather than proof of reproducibility.The external Diamond installation, mutable base image documentation.   * - Documentation     - Strict Sphinx builds, SVG/PDF exports and offline Chromium checks of embedded diagrams and waveform controls.These comparisons concern rebuilt legacy projects,       """Generate program pages from fresh RTL schematics and passing simulations."""
      import json
      from pathlib import Path
      import shutil
      import subprocess
      import sys
      
      from toolchain.analysis.netlist import ROOT, export_netlist
      from toolchain.analysis.waveform import write_waveform
      from toolchain.buildsystem.model import BuildError, load_build
      from toolchain.buildsystem.workflow import digest, write_json
      
      
      def generate(root=ROOT):
          """Build documentation assets for every program manifest, including clones."""
          generated = root / 'docs/_generated'
          if generated.is_symlink():
              raise BuildError('Generated documentation directory must not be a symlink')
          if generated.exists():
              shutil.rmtree(generated)
          pages = generated / 'programs'
          pages.mkdir(parents=True)
          names = sorted(p.parent.name for p in (root / 'programs').glob('*/*.toml')
                         if p.stem == p.parent.name)
          if not names:
              raise BuildError('No program manifests found')
          for name in names:
              build = load_build(root, name)
              netlist = export_netlist(build)
              before = {str(p.relative_to(root)): digest(p) for p in (*[s.path for s in build.sources], build.testbench)}
              subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', 'toolchain/simulation/test_simulation.py',
                              '--program', name, '--wave-format', 'vcd', '--seed', '1', '-q'], cwd=root, check=True)
              if before != {str(p.relative_to(root)): digest(p) for p in (*[s.path for s in build.sources], build.testbench)}:
                  raise BuildError(f'{name}: sources changed while generating documentation')
              net_inputs = json.loads((netlist / 'netlist.json').read_text())['inputs']
              if any(before[path] != value for path, value in net_inputs.items()):
                  raise BuildError(f'{name}: netlist and simulation use different HDL')
              simulation = build.build_root / 'simulation'
              run = json.loads((simulation / 'run.json').read_text())
              info = write_waveform(simulation / 'waves.vcd', simulation / 'waveform.html',
                                    f'{name} — RTL waveform', run['simulation_duration_ns'])
              write_json(simulation / 'waveform.json', {**info, 'inputs': before,
                         'vcd_sha256': digest(simulation / 'waves.vcd'), 'seed': 1})
              assets = generated / 'static/program-assets' / name
              assets.mkdir(parents=True)
              for src in [netlist / 'netlist.svg', netlist / 'netlist.pdf', netlist / 'netlist.json',
                          simulation / 'waveform.html', simulation / 'waves.vcd',
                          simulation / 'waveform.json', simulation / 'run.json']:
                  shutil.copy2(src, assets / src.name)
              intro = root / 'programs' / name / 'description.rst'
              description = (f'.. include:: ../../../programs/{name}/description.rst\n\n' if intro.is_file()
                             else 'This page is generated from the program manifest, HDL and cocotb testbench.\n\n')
              page = f'''{name}
      {'=' * len(name)}
      
      {description}Target: ``{build.target}``; top entity: ``{build.top}``.
      
      RTL netlist
      -----------
      
      This is a generic RTL schematic produced by GHDL synthesis, Yosys process
      lowering/flattening and Graphviz. It does not apply LPF constraints or reproduce
      Diamond technology mapping, placement, routing or timing. Vendor-specific
      attributes may be ignored; warnings are retained in the program's netlist logs.
      
      .. image:: ../static/program-assets/{name}/netlist.svg
         :alt: Generic RTL netlist for {name}
         :width: 100%
         :target: ../../program-assets/{name}/netlist.svg
      
      Download :download:`SVG <../static/program-assets/{name}/netlist.svg>`,
      :download:`PDF <../static/program-assets/{name}/netlist.pdf>` or
      :download:`netlist provenance <../static/program-assets/{name}/netlist.json>`.
      
      Simulation waveform
      -------------------
      
      The program's actual cocotb testbench passed. This trace covers
      **{info['duration_ns']:g} ns** of simulated time and **{info['signal_count']} signals**.
      Choose a channel, zoom in by dragging, and hover to read exact values.
      Unknown and high-impedance values appear at mid-level, not as logic zero.
      The viewer includes Plotly locally and works without an internet connection.
      
      .. only:: html
      
         .. raw:: html
      
            <iframe src="../../program-assets/{name}/waveform.html" title="{name} simulation waveform" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:1px solid #ddd" loading="lazy"></iframe>
      
      Download the :download:`interactive waveform <../static/program-assets/{name}/waveform.html>`,
      :download:`VCD trace <../static/program-assets/{name}/waves.vcd>`,
      :download:`simulation provenance <../static/program-assets/{name}/run.json>` or
      :download:`waveform provenance <../static/program-assets/{name}/waveform.json>`.
      The VCD contains the regression stimulus, not an application example or a
      post-route timing simulation. VCD records timestamped values, not VHDL delta cycles.
      
      Testbench
      ---------
      
      .. literalinclude:: ../../../programs/{name}/{name}_tb.py
         :language: python
      '''
              (pages / f'program-{name}.rst').write_text(page)
          (pages / 'index.rst').write_text('Programs\n========\n\n'
              'Each page combines the authored description with freshly generated netlist and simulation evidence.\n\n'
              '.. toctree::\n   :maxdepth: 1\n\n' + ''.join(f'   program-{name}\n' for name in names))
          return pages
      
      
      def main():
          try:
              print(generate())
          except (BuildError, OSError, ValueError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as exc:
              print(f'Program documentation failed: {exc}', file=sys.stderr)
              return 1
          return 0
      
      
      if __name__ == '__main__':
          raise SystemExit(main())
      .DEFAULT_GOAL := build
      PYTHON ?= python3
      TARGET ?= uz_dslot_xo2
      TEMPLATE ?= tx30
      # Quote values as single shell arguments, including embedded apostrophes.
      quote = '$(subst ','"'"',$(1))'
      ARGS = --target $(call quote,$(TARGET)) $(if $(PROGRAM),--program $(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) $(if $(TOOLCHAIN),--toolchain $(call quote,$(TOOLCHAIN)))
      .PHONY: build list doctor new check project gui build-all clean test docs docs-local docs-assets-local netlist netlist-local sim sim-image sim-container test-container docs-container _sim
      build list doctor check project gui build-all:
      	$(PYTHON) -m toolchain.buildsystem $@ $(ARGS)
      new:
      	$(PYTHON) -m toolchain.buildsystem new $(ARGS) --name $(call quote,$(NAME)) --template $(call quote,$(TEMPLATE))
      clean:
      	$(PYTHON) -m toolchain.buildsystem clean $(ARGS) $(if $(filter 1,$(DISCARD_PROJECT_CHANGES)),--discard-project-changes)
      test:
      	$(PYTHON) -m unittest discover -s toolchain/tests -v
      CONTAINER_ENGINE ?= docker
      CONTAINER_PLATFORM ?= linux/amd64
      CONTAINER_USERNS = $(if $(filter podman,$(notdir $(CONTAINER_ENGINE))),--userns=keep-id)
      SIM_IMAGE ?= uz-cpld-toolchain
      # Bind source for commands run from the host.
      SIM_WORKSPACE ?= $(CURDIR)
      SEED ?= 1
      WAVE_FORMAT ?= vcd
      CONTAINER_RUN = $(CONTAINER_ENGINE) run --rm --platform $(call quote,$(CONTAINER_PLATFORM)) $(CONTAINER_USERNS) --user "$$(id -u):$$(id -g)" --mount $(call quote,type=bind$(comma)source=$(SIM_WORKSPACE)$(comma)target=/work) -w /work $(call quote,$(SIM_IMAGE))
      comma := ,
      sim-image:
      	@command -v $(CONTAINER_ENGINE) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Container engine missing. Install Docker on the host or reopen in the unified Dev Container." >&2; exit 1; }
      	$(CONTAINER_ENGINE) build --platform $(call quote,$(CONTAINER_PLATFORM)) --target toolchain -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile -t $(call quote,$(SIM_IMAGE)) .
      ifeq ($(CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER),1)
      sim: _sim
      test-container: test
      docs: docs-local
      netlist: netlist-local
      else
      sim: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make _sim $(if $(PROGRAM),PROGRAM=$(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) SEED=$(call quote,$(SEED)) WAVE_FORMAT=$(call quote,$(WAVE_FORMAT))
      test-container: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make test
      netlist: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make netlist-local $(if $(PROGRAM),PROGRAM=$(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) TARGET=$(call quote,$(TARGET))
      docs: sim-image
      	$(CONTAINER_RUN) make docs-local
      endif
      # Compatibility alias.
      sim-container: sim
      docs-container: docs
      # Image-internal entry point. Never creates or selects a host virtual environment.
      _sim:
      	@test "$(CPLD_TOOLCHAIN_CONTAINER)" = "1" || { echo "Use 'make sim' to run in the simulation container." >&2; exit 1; }
      	python3 -m pytest toolchain/simulation/test_simulation.py -v --junitxml=toolchain/build/simulation/junit.xml $(if $(PROGRAM),--program $(call quote,$(PROGRAM))) --seed $(call quote,$(SEED)) --wave-format $(call quote,$(WAVE_FORMAT))
      netlist-local:
      	$(PYTHON) -m toolchain.analysis.netlist --target $(call quote,$(TARGET)) $(if $(PROGRAM),--program $(call quote,$(PROGRAM)))
      docs-assets-local:
      	$(PYTHON) -m toolchain.analysis.documentation
      docs-local: docs-assets-local
      	$(PYTHON) -m sphinx -W --keep-going -b html docs docs/_build/html

      Build and publish documentation
      ===============================
      
      Local build
      -----------
      
      ::
      
         make docs
      
      The host command builds the ``toolchain`` image and runs simulation, netlist analysis and Sphinx inside it without Diamond, license mounts, host networking or developer CLI installation.
      Inside a Dev Container, the command uses installed tools directly.
      ``make docs-container`` is an alias, and ``make docs-local`` explicitly selects native tools.
      Dependencies come from ``docs/requirements.txt`` and its referenced files in both the image and native setup.
      
      The complete site is ``docs/_build/html/``; it includes SVGs, PDFs, VCD downloads and self-contained waveform HTML.
      Relative links support repository subpaths such as ``/uz_cpld/``.
      The Sphinx GitHub Pages extension writes ``.nojekyll`` so underscore-prefixed assets are preserved when served through Pages.
      Each build clears the HTML output to prevent removed pages or archived transcripts from remaining in a published site.
      
      GitHub Pages
      ------------
      
      The repository workflow ``.github/workflows/toolchain.yml`` builds the image, runs tooling tests and generates documentation in separate steps.
      Pull requests and branch pushes produce review artifacts without publishing.
      Successful pushes or manual runs on the repository's default branch upload a Pages artifact and deploy through the ``github-pages`` environment.
      The default-branch condition follows repository metadata rather than assuming a branch name.
      
      Enable **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions** once in the GitHub repository.
      Allow the default branch in the ``github-pages`` environment and satisfy any repository approval rules.
      The deployment job uses ``pages: write`` and ``id-token: write``; the build job needs only read access to repository contents.
      The deployment URL appears in the workflow's environment result, with ``https://ultrazohm.github.io/uz_cpld/`` as the standard project-site address unless repository settings specify a custom domain.
      
      The workflow uploads only the generated HTML site for deployment, retaining build diagnostics separately.
      It does not compile or publish firmware.
      A configured workflow is not evidence of a successful hosted deployment; verify the GitHub Actions run after merging it.
      
      Maintenance
      -----------
      
      Keep prose concise and factual, with tradeoffs in :doc:`architecture` and open work in :doc:`roadmap`.
      Use one sentence per RST source line with no manual wrapping; code blocks and directive/table syntax retain their required structure.
      README files point to this Sphinx project rather than duplicating instructions.
      OS packages and the base image tag are mutable; pinning image digests and package snapshots improves reproducibility at the cost of an explicit update process.
      
      References
      ----------
      
      * `GitHub Pages custom workflows <https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages>`_
      * `Sphinx GitHub Pages extension <https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/extensions/githubpages.html>`_
